title.zh: 卷347 列傳一百三十四 杨遇春子：国桢 吴廷刚 祝廷彪 游栋雲 罗思举 桂涵 包相卿
title.en: Volume 347 Biographies 134: Yang Yuchun son: Guo Zhen, Wu Tinggang, Zhu Tingbiao, You Dongyun, Luo Siju, Gui Han, Bao Xiangqing
title.raw: 卷347 列傳一百三十四 杨遇春子：国桢 吴廷刚 祝廷彪 游栋雲 罗思举 桂涵 包相卿

sentences.zh: 楊遇春，字時齋，四川崇慶人。

translations.literal: Yang Yuchun, style name Shizhai, was a man of Chongqing in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuchun, whose courtesy name was Shizhai, came from Chongqing in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 以武舉效用督標，為福康安所識拔。

translations.literal: By the military examination he entered service in the provincial commander's standard and was recognized and promoted by Fuk'anggan.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service through the military examination in the provincial commander's corps and was discovered and advanced by Fuk'anggan.

sentences.zh: 從征甘肅石峰堡、台灣、廓爾喀，咸有功，累擢守備。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns to Shifeng Fort in Gansu, Taiwan, and Gurkha, distinguishing himself in each, and was repeatedly promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in expeditions against Shifeng Fort in Gansu, in Taiwan, and against Gurkha, earning distinction in each and rising in stages to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六十年，調赴苗疆，力戰解嗅腦圍，進援松桃，獨取道樟桂溪，山險寨密，率敢死四十人為前鋒，由間道縱馬入賊屯，呼曰：「大兵至矣！

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year of Qianlong he was transferred to the Miao frontier, fought fiercely to relieve the siege of Xiunao, advanced to relieve Songtao, alone took the route through Zhangguixi where mountains were perilous and stockades dense, led forty dare-to-die men as vanguard, by a hidden path spurred horses into the rebel stockade, and cried: "The great army has arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year of the Qianlong reign (1795), he was posted to the Miao borderlands. After fierce fighting he lifted the siege of Xiunao, then marched to relieve Songtao. He alone took the route through Zhangguixi, where the mountains were steep and stockades thick. At the head of forty volunteers he charged along a secret track into the rebel camp and shouted, "The imperial army is here!"

sentences.zh: 降者免死。

translations.literal: Those who surrender will be spared death.
translations.idiomatic: Surrender and you will live.

sentences.zh: 」賊相顧錯愕；

translations.literal: " The rebels looked at one another in dismay;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels stared at one another in confusion;

sentences.zh: 复呼曰：「降者跪！

translations.literal: again he cried: "Those who surrender kneel!"
translations.idiomatic: he shouted again, "Kneel if you surrender!"

sentences.zh: 」於是跪者數千人，直抵城下，圍遂解，賜花翎。

translations.literal: " Thus several thousand knelt, advanced straight to beneath the walls, the siege was then lifted, and he was awarded the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands knelt at once and marched straight to the city gate; the siege was broken, and he received the peacock-plume insignia.

sentences.zh: 复解永綏圍，賜號勁勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Again he relieved the siege of Yongshun and was granted the title Vigorous Brave Batu.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted the siege of Yongshun as well and was granted the title of Valiant Brave Batu.

sentences.zh: 首逆吳半生就擒，擢游擊。

translations.literal: The principal rebel Wu Bansheng was captured, and he was promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: The chief rebel Wu Bansheng was taken, and Yuchun was promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 額勒登保攻茶山，為賊所圍；

translations.literal: Ereldunbao attacked Chashan and was surrounded by rebels;
translations.idiomatic: When Ereldunbao assaulted Chashan, the rebels surrounded him;

sentences.zh: 遇春率壯士衝擊，奪據對山，縱橫決盪，當者輒靡。

translations.literal: Yuchun led stalwarts in a charge, seized the opposing hill, swept back and forth decisively, and whoever stood in his way was scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchun led picked troops in a charge, seized the hill opposite, and cut through the enemy ranks so that all who faced him broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 福康安望之驚嘆，立擢參將。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan watched in astonished admiration and immediately promoted him to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan, watching from afar, cried out in wonder and promoted him on the spot to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 复乾州，擢廣東羅定協副將。

translations.literal: He again recovered Qianzhou and was promoted to deputy commander of the Luoding garrison in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Qianzhou and was made deputy commander of the Luoding garrison in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 苗平而教匪起，嘉慶二年，從額勒登保赴湖北剿覃加耀、林之華，破芭葉山，連敗之長陽、宣恩、建始、恩施。

translations.literal: When the Miao were pacified the sect rebels rose; in the second year of Jiaqing he followed Ereldunbao to Hubei to suppress Tan Jiayao and Lin Zhihua, broke Baye Mountain, and repeatedly defeated them at Changyang, Xuan'en, Jianshi, and Enshi.
translations.idiomatic: After the Miao rebellion was settled, the White Lotus rebels erupted. In the second year of Jiaqing (1797) he followed Ereldunbao to Hubei against Tan Jiayao and Lin Zhihua, stormed Baye Mountain, and routed them again and again at Changyang, Xuan'en, Jianshi, and Enshi.

sentences.zh: 加耀竄終報寨，峭岩陡絕，夜縋而登，擒加耀及其黨張正潮。

translations.literal: Jiayao fled to Zhongbao stockade on sheer cliffs impossible to scale; at night they were lowered on ropes to climb and captured Jiayao and his partisan Zhang Zhengchao.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayao fled to Zhongbao stockade, perched on cliffs so steep they seemed unreachable; Yuchun's men climbed by rope in the night and took Jiayao and his lieutenant Zhang Zhengchao.

sentences.zh: 三年，從額勒登保赴陝，敗李全於藍田，又敗高均德於紫溪嶺。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Ereldunbao to Shaanxi, defeated Li Quan at Lantian, and again defeated Gao Junde at Zixi Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1798) he marched with Ereldunbao into Shaanxi, defeated Li Quan at Lantian, and routed Gao Junde at Zixi Ridge.

sentences.zh: 五月，還湖北。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he returned to Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifth month he was back in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 張漢潮竄穀城，兜擊，大敗之，又敗之竹山菩提河，追躡入陝，敗之於平利孟石嶺。

translations.literal: Zhang Hanchao fled to Gucheng; Yuchun intercepted and routed him, again defeated him at Puti River in Zhushan, pursued into Shaanxi, and defeated him at Mengshi Ridge in Pingli.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hanchao fled to Gucheng, Yuchun cut him off and inflicted a crushing defeat, beat him again at Puti River in Zhushan, chased him into Shaanxi, and defeated him once more at Mengshi Ridge in Pingli.

sentences.zh: 九月，敗高均德、李全於廣元吳家河。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he defeated Gao Junde and Li Quan at Wujia River in Guangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he routed Gao Junde and Li Quan at Wujia River in Guangyuan.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，賜金治喪，命墨絰隨徵。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father; gold was granted for the funeral and he was ordered to wear unbleached hemp while continuing on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he was granted funds for the funeral but ordered to remain on campaign in mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 迭破羅其清於觀音坪、大鵬寨、青觀山，其清就擒，擢甘肅西寧鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated Luo Qiqing at Guanyin Flat, Dapeng stockade, and Qingguan Mountain; Qiqing was captured, and Yuchun was promoted to commander of the Xining garrison in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He beat Luo Qiqing again and again at Guanyin Flat, Dapeng stockade, and Qingguan Mountain until Qiqing was taken, and Yuchun was made commander of the Xining garrison in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 四年，從額勒登保斬蕭佔國、張長庚，獲王光祖，斃冷天祿，功皆最​​，威震川、陝，婦孺皆知其名。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed Ereldunbao in beheading Xiao Zhanguo and Zhang Changgeng, capturing Wang Guangzu, and killing Leng Tianlu; his merit ranked foremost, his fame shook Sichuan and Shaanxi, and women and children all knew his name.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1799) he served under Ereldunbao in killing Xiao Zhanguo and Zhang Changgeng, capturing Wang Guangzu, and slaying Leng Tianlu. His achievements topped the rolls, his renown filled Sichuan and Shaanxi, and even children knew his name.

sentences.zh: 追剿張子聰，自夏徂秋，迭敗之於梁山、雲陽、太平、開縣、通江間。

translations.literal: Pursuing Zhang Zicong from summer through autumn, he repeatedly defeated him between Liangshan, Yunyang, Taiping, Kaixian, and Tongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted Zhang Zicong from summer into autumn and routed him again and again across Liangshan, Yunyang, Taiping, Kaixian, and Tongjiang.

sentences.zh: 子聰被追急，數與樊人傑、龔建、冉天元合，最後欲合王登廷。

translations.literal: Zicong, pressed hard in pursuit, several times joined Fan Renjie, Gong Jian, and Ran Tianyuan, and at last sought to unite with Wang Dengting.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Zicong repeatedly joined forces with Fan Renjie, Gong Jian, and Ran Tianyuan and finally tried to link up with Wang Dengting.

sentences.zh: 登廷踞馬鞍寨，進攻克之，躡追迭擊，擒其黨靳有年於土丫子，斬阮正漋於廣元雲霧山。

translations.literal: Dengting held Ma'an stockade; Yuchun advanced and stormed it, pursued and struck repeatedly, captured his partisan Jin Younian at Tuyazi, and beheaded Ruan Zhengchong at Yunwu Mountain in Guangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dengting held Ma'an stockade; Yuchun stormed it, harried the fleeing rebels, took his lieutenant Jin Younian at Tuyazi, and cut down Ruan Zhengchong on Yunwu Mountain in Guangyuan.

sentences.zh: 至冬，登廷由陝入川，與冉天元合。

translations.literal: By winter Dengting entered Sichuan from Shaanxi and joined Ran Tianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When winter came, Dengting crossed from Shaanxi into Sichuan and united with Ran Tianyuan.

sentences.zh: 額勒登保率遇春與穆克登布會擊之於蒼溪貓兒埡。

translations.literal: Ereldunbao led Yuchun and Mukedengbu in a joint attack on them at Mao'erya in Cangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ereldunbao led Yuchun and Mukedengbu to strike them together at Mao'erya in Cangxi.

sentences.zh: 穆克登布違約，先期進，挫敗，遇春據廢壘力拒，燃草炬擲山下，戰徹夜，幸得全師，迭擊皆獲勝。

translations.literal: Mukedengbu broke agreement and advanced ahead of time, was defeated; Yuchun held an abandoned rampart and resisted fiercely, lit grass torches and hurled them down the slope, fought through the night, fortunately preserved his force intact, and in successive attacks always won.
translations.idiomatic: Mukedengbu broke the plan and attacked early, only to be beaten back. Yuchun held a ruined fort and fought on, flinging burning grass torches down the slope. The battle lasted all night; he kept his army intact and won every clash that followed.

sentences.zh: 登廷孑身至蒲江，為鄉團擒獻，斬之。

translations.literal: Dengting alone reached Pujiang, was seized and presented by local militia, and was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Dengting fled alone to Pujiang, where local militia seized him and handed him over; he was then executed.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢甘州提督，偕穆克登布破張天倫於兩當，又從額勒登保追楊開甲於商、雒，扼龍駒寨，殲張漢潮餘黨劉允恭、劉開玉，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to commander at Ganzhou, with Mukedengbu defeated Zhang Tianlun at Liangdang, again followed Ereldunbao in pursuing Yang Kaijia in Shang and Luo, blocked Longju stockade, annihilated Zhang Hanchao's remnant partisans Liu Yungong and Liu Kaiyu, and was granted a hereditary yunqiwei rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1800) he became commander at Ganzhou. With Mukedengbu he broke Zhang Tianlun at Liangdang, then followed Ereldunbao in chasing Yang Kaijia through Shang and Luo, sealed Longju stockade, and wiped out Zhang Hanchao's lieutenants Liu Yungong and Liu Kaiyu. He received a hereditary yunqiwei commission.

sentences.zh: 遇春與穆克登佈為經略左、右翼長，議每不合，自蒼溪戰後，益不相能。

translations.literal: Yuchun and Mukedengbu were left and right wing commanders under the grand coordinator; their counsel never agreed, and after the Cangxi battle they were even less able to cooperate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchun and Mukedengbu served as the grand coordinator's left and right wing commanders but rarely agreed. After the battle at Cangxi they could hardly work together at all.

sentences.zh: 額勒登保等疏言：「諸將中惟遇春謀勇兼優，可當一面。

translations.literal: Ereldunbao and others memorialized: "Among the generals only Yuchun combines strategy and courage and can hold a front alone."
translations.idiomatic: Ereldunbao and others wrote to the throne: "Of all the generals, only Yuchun has both counsel and courage and can command a theater on his own."

sentences.zh: 請益所部兵，與經略、參贊分路勦賊。

translations.literal: We ask to increase his troops so that he, the grand coordinator, and the commissioner may suppress rebels by separate routes."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that his force be enlarged so he, the grand coordinator, and the commissioner can hunt the rebels on separate lines."

sentences.zh: 」遂以提督別領偏師，沿渭西上，剿汧、隴之賊。

translations.literal: " Thereupon as commander he separately led a detached column west along the Wei to suppress rebels in Qian and Long.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved, and as commander he led a detached column up the west bank of the Wei to clear rebels from Qian and Long.

sentences.zh: 五月，擊伍金柱於漢陰手板岩及銅錢窖，戰方酣，楊開甲從間道突至，腹背受敵，自午至酉，圍愈急，有白袍賊手大旗，直犯遇春，相去咫尺，忽墜馬，則為後隊護槍所斃，乃金柱悍黨龐洪勝也。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he attacked Wu Jinzhu at Shouban Rock and Tongqian cellar in Hanyin; battle was fierce when Yang Kaijia burst in by a hidden path, and he was attacked front and rear from noon to dusk as the encirclement tightened. A white-robed rebel bearing a great banner charged straight at Yuchun; within a pace the man suddenly fell from his horse, shot dead by rear-guard musketeers — he was Pang Hongsheng, Jinzhu's fierce partisan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he struck Wu Jinzhu at Shouban Rock and Tongqian cellar in Hanyin. While the fight was hottest, Yang Kaijia hit him from a side path, and from noon until evening Yuchun was caught between two fires. A rebel in white robes carrying a great banner charged straight at him; within a step the man fell from his horse, killed by rear-guard musketeers — Pang Hongsheng, Jinzhu's fiercest lieutenant.

sentences.zh: 賊驚潰，額勒登保兵亦會，追賊至洋縣茅坪，斬開甲，又擒陳杰於大石坂。

translations.literal: The rebels fled in panic; Ereldunbao's troops also joined, pursued the rebels to Maoping in Yangxian, beheaded Kaijia, and again captured Chen Jie at Dashiban.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke and ran. Ereldunbao's men came up, and together they chased the enemy to Maoping in Yangxian, where Kaijia was killed and Chen Jie was taken at Dashiban.

sentences.zh: 八月，斬金柱於成縣峽溝，斬宋麻子於鳳縣潘家溝。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he beheaded Jinzhu at Xiagou in Chengxian and Song Mazi at Panjiagou in Fengxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he killed Jinzhu at Xiagou in Chengxian and Song Mazi at Panjiagou in Fengxian.

sentences.zh: 六年，破冉學勝於石泉石塔寺。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he defeated Ran Xuesheng at Shita Temple in Shiquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1801) he routed Ran Xuesheng at Shita Temple in Shiquan.

sentences.zh: 高天德、馬學禮、王廷詔為大軍所驅，竄五郎壩。

translations.literal: Gao Tiande, Ma Xueli, and Wang Tingzhao, driven by the main army, fled to Wulangba.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tiande, Ma Xueli, and Wang Tingzhao, harried by the main force, fled to Wulangba.

sentences.zh: 遇春方追學勝，偵知之，乘夜掩擊，天德等分竄，乃由斜峪關躡擊，阻其入甘肅之路，复破賊於鋼鋪廠，一晝夜馳四百里，追及廷詔於川、陝界鞍子溝擒之，天德、學禮竄禪家岩。

translations.literal: Yuchun was pursuing Xuesheng when he learned of this by reconnaissance, made a night assault, and Tiande and the others scattered; he then pursued through Xieyu Pass, blocked their road into Gansu, again defeated rebels at Gangpu factory, rode four hundred li in a day and night, overtook Tingzhao at Anzigou on the Sichuan-Shaanxi border and captured him, while Tiande and Xueli fled to Chanjiayan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchun was chasing Xuesheng when scouts brought word of the three rebels. He struck by night; Tiande and the others split up. He pressed through Xieyu Pass to cut off their escape into Gansu, beat them again at Gangpu factory, rode four hundred li in a single day and night, and overtook Tingzhao at Anzigou on the Sichuan-Shaanxi border and took him. Tiande and Xueli fled to Chanjiayan.

sentences.zh: 遇春料賊由寧羌奔逸，急由斜谷趨二郎壩，設伏龍洞溪，賊果至，俘斬殆盡，二賊就擒，晉騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: Yuchun judged the rebels would flee through Ningqiang, hurried by Xiegu toward Erlangba, set an ambush at Longdong Stream; the rebels came as expected, were nearly all captured or killed, the two rebels were taken, and he was advanced to hereditary cavalry commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Expecting them to flee through Ningqiang, Yuchun raced through Xiegu to Erlangba and laid an ambush at Longdong Stream. The rebels came as he foresaw; nearly all were killed or captured, and both Tiande and Xueli were taken. He was promoted to hereditary cavalry commandant.

sentences.zh: 是役，釋降眾健者八百人，編為一隊，皆原效死。

translations.literal: In this campaign he released eight hundred sturdy men from among the surrendered masses, organized them as one company, and all volunteered to die in his service.
translations.idiomatic: After this fight he enrolled eight hundred fit men from among the surrendered rebels in a single company; every one of them volunteered to fight to the death for him.

sentences.zh: 會經略檄合剿冉學勝，獲諜，得賊虛實，謂降眾曰：「汝等立功贖罪，此其時矣！

translations.literal: When the grand coordinator's order came for a joint campaign against Ran Xuesheng, he obtained a spy and learned the rebels' true situation, and said to the surrendered men: "You may earn merit to redeem your guilt — now is the time!"
translations.idiomatic: When orders came for a joint strike on Ran Xuesheng, a spy told him the enemy's dispositions. He told the surrendered troops, "Here is your chance to win merit and wipe away your crimes!"

sentences.zh: 」至紫陽天池山，賊於伏莽中突起，八百人力戰，衝賊為數段，遂大捷。

translations.literal: " At Tianchi Mountain in Ziyang the rebels sprang up from ambush in the thickets; the eight hundred fought fiercely, broke the rebels into several segments, and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianchi Mountain in Ziyang the rebels rose from ambush in the brush. The eight hundred fought hand to hand, shattered the enemy into several bands, and won a resounding victory.

sentences.zh: 張天倫糾五路賊聚洵陽，學勝復與合，大破之於孫家坡。

translations.literal: Zhang Tianlun gathered rebels from five routes at Xunyang; Xuesheng again joined him, and Yuchun routed them at Sunjiapo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianlun mustered rebels from five routes at Xunyang. Xuesheng joined him again, and Yuchun crushed them at Sunjiapo.

sentences.zh: 追賊入川，擒冉天泗、王士虎於通江報曉埡。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rebels into Sichuan, he captured Ran Tiansi and Wang Shihu at Baoxiao'ya in Tongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He chased the rebels into Sichuan and took Ran Tiansi and Wang Shihu at Baoxiao'ya in Tongjiang.

sentences.zh: 士虎故劇盜，專劫寨峒避大軍。

translations.literal: Shihu had been a notorious bandit who specialized in raiding stockades and cave villages to avoid the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Shihu was a notorious bandit who preyed on stockades and cave hamlets to keep clear of the main columns.

sentences.zh: 遇春夜往捕，適賊由他路襲營，遇春不回救，伏巢外候賊歸，擒斬無遺。

translations.literal: Yuchun went by night to capture him; the rebels happened to attack the camp by another route, but Yuchun did not return to relieve it, lay in ambush outside their lair awaiting their return, and captured and killed them to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchun went out by night to seize him. Rebels struck the camp by another road, but he did not turn back; he waited in ambush outside their den until they returned and killed or captured every one of them.

sentences.zh: 賊中有名號者剿除幾盡，餘匪以老林為藪。

translations.literal: Rebels with known names were nearly all exterminated; the remainder took the old forests as their refuge.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly every rebel of note had been wiped out; the survivors hid in the deep old-growth forests.

sentences.zh: 遇春專任搜剿，以遲緩，嚴詔切責。

translations.literal: Yuchun was solely charged with search and suppression; for slowness he received stern edicts of sharp rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchun alone was charged with hunting them down, and when progress lagged the court sent stern rebukes.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，殲苟文明，調固原提督。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year he annihilated Gou Wenming and was transferred to commander at Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year (1802) he destroyed Gou Wenming and was posted as commander at Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 尋以大功戡定，詔遇春功尤著，殲首逆獨多，晉二等輕車都尉。

translations.literal: Soon, with great merit the rebellion was settled; an edict said Yuchun's achievement was especially outstanding and he alone had destroyed the most principal rebels, and he was advanced to second-class light chariot commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the great campaign ended in victory, an edict singled out Yuchun's outstanding service — he alone had killed more rebel chiefs than any other — and promoted him to second-class light chariot commandant.

sentences.zh: 八年，丁母憂，賜金，給假四十日。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered mourning for his mother; gold was granted and forty days' leave given.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1803) his mother died; the court granted funds for the funeral and forty days' leave.

sentences.zh: 苟文明餘黨苟文潤集千餘人，皆獷悍，蹂躪漢江左右，諸軍久役不振。

translations.literal: Gou Wenming's remnant partisan Gou Wenrun gathered more than a thousand men, all fierce and brutal, ravaging both banks of the Han River; the various armies, long on campaign, could not rouse themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Wenming's lieutenant Gou Wenrun rallied more than a thousand hardened fighters who ravaged both banks of the Han. The other armies, worn down by years of campaigning, could not shake them off.

sentences.zh: 遇春至，乃奮，連戰紅山寺、平溪河，殲之，賊氛漸清。

translations.literal: When Yuchun arrived they roused themselves, fought continuously at Hongshan Temple and Pingxi River, annihilated them, and the rebel atmosphere gradually cleared.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchun arrived his men found new heart. He fought them at Hongshan Temple and Pingxi River in succession, destroyed them, and the rebellion along the Han began to subside.

sentences.zh: 十年，凱撤，詔許回籍補持母服百日，假滿入覲。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the victory forces withdrew; an edict permitted him to return home to complete the hundred days of mourning for his mother, and when leave ended he entered audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1805) the victorious armies were withdrawn. He was allowed to go home and complete the hundred days of mourning for his mother, then return to court when his leave ended.

sentences.zh: 會寧陝鎮兵變。

translations.literal: It happened that the Ningshan garrison troops mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Ningshan garrison mutinied.

sentences.zh: 鎮兵新設，入伍者多鄉勇、降賊，不易制。

translations.literal: The garrison troops were newly established; many who entered service were local militia and surrendered rebels, not easy to control.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison was newly formed, filled largely with local militia and former rebels, and proved hard to discipline.

sentences.zh: 總兵楊芳赴固原攝提督，因停給鹽米銀，發包穀充糧，遂戕副將、游擊，劫庫獄以叛。

translations.literal: Commander Yang Fang went to Guyuan to act as commander in the commander's absence; because payment of salt-rice silver was stopped and bagged grain was issued as rations, they killed the deputy commander and regional commander, plundered the treasury and prison, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Yang Fang had gone to Guyuan to act as interim commander. When salt-and-rice stipends were cut and the men were paid in bagged grain instead, they murdered the deputy and regional commanders, looted the treasury and jail, and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 遇春行至西安，聞變，偕巡撫方維甸馳往。

translations.literal: Yuchun had reached Xi'an, heard of the mutiny, and hurried there with Governor Fang Weidian.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchun was at Xi'an when he heard the news and rode at once to the scene with Governor Fang Weidian.

sentences.zh: 詔德楞泰赴陝治其事，命遇春扼方柴關，賊銳甚，兵交數失利。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Delengtai to Shaanxi to handle the affair and commanded Yuchun to hold Fangchai Pass; the rebels were very sharp, and in several engagements the troops suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Delengtai was ordered to Shaanxi to handle the crisis while Yuchun blocked Fangchai Pass. The mutineers fought fiercely and the government troops lost several skirmishes.

sentences.zh: 賊首蒲大芳望見遇春，下馬遙跪，哭訴營官蝕餉狀，遇春曉以順逆，知可以義動，與楊芳謀，同主撫。

translations.literal: The rebel leader Pu Dafang saw Yuchun, dismounted and knelt from afar, weeping as he told how camp officers embezzled rations; Yuchun enlightened him on loyalty and rebellion, knew he could be moved by righteousness, consulted with Yang Fang, and both favored pacification.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chief Pu Dafang saw Yuchun, dismounted, and knelt at a distance, weeping as he described how officers had stolen their pay. Yuchun reasoned with him about loyalty and treason, judged that he could be swayed by justice, and with Yang Fang agreed on a policy of pacification.

sentences.zh: 諸帥尚猶豫，遇春按兵緩攻，令芳單騎入賊營諭之。

translations.literal: The various commanders still hesitated; Yuchun held his troops and attacked slowly, and ordered Fang to enter the rebel camp alone on horseback to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Other commanders still wavered. Yuchun held his army back and pressed lightly, then sent Fang alone into the rebel camp to parley.

sentences.zh: 越數日，大芳竟縛倡逆之陳達順、陳先倫詣遇春降。

translations.literal: After several days Dafang actually bound the instigators of rebellion Chen Dashun and Chen Xianlun and came to Yuchun to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Dafang bound the ringleaders Chen Dashun and Chen Xianlun and brought them to Yuchun to surrender.

sentences.zh: 遂率大芳邀擊餘賊於江口，斬其渠硃先貴。

translations.literal: He then led Dafang to intercept the remaining rebels at Jiangkou and beheaded their leader Zhu Xiangui.
translations.idiomatic: He then led Dafang in an ambush of the remaining rebels at Jiangkou and killed their leader Zhu Xiangui.

sentences.zh: 德楞泰疏陳叛兵窮蹙乞命，請釋歸伍，詔斥縱叛廢法，降遇春寧陝鎮總兵，大芳等二百餘人皆戍新疆。

translations.literal: Delengtai memorialized that the mutineers, driven to extremity, begged for their lives and asked that they be released back to the ranks; an edict rebuked indulgence toward rebels and abandonment of law, demoted Yuchun to commander of the Ningshan garrison, and more than two hundred men including Dafang were all exiled to garrison Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Delengtai reported that the mutineers, cornered, pleaded for mercy and asked to be restored to the ranks. The throne rebuked leniency toward rebels as a breach of law, demoted Yuchun to commander of the Ningshan garrison, and sent Dafang and more than two hundred others to exile in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 十三年，入覲，命兼乾清門侍衛，仍授固原提督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he entered audience, was ordered to serve concurrently as attendant of the Qianqing Gate, and was again appointed commander at Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (1808) he came to court, was made an attendant of the Qianqing Gate, and was restored as commander at Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 十八年，天理教匪李文成踞滑縣，命陝甘總督那彥成討之，以遇春為參贊。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Tianli sect rebel Li Wencheng held Huaxian; the Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general Nayancheng was ordered to suppress him, with Yuchun as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1813) the Tianli sect rebel Li Wencheng seized Huaxian. Governor-General Nayancheng of Shaanxi and Gansu was sent against him with Yuchun as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 賊萃精銳道口鎮，遇春率親兵八十人，沿運河西進覘之，遇賊數千，即突擊，賊辟易，追渡河，擒斬二百；

translations.literal: The rebels massed elite troops at Daokou Town; Yuchun led eighty personal guards west along the Grand Canal to reconnoiter, met several thousand rebels, immediately charged, the rebels gave way, pursued across the river, and captured or killed two hundred;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels concentrated their best troops at Daokou Town. Yuchun took eighty personal guards up the Grand Canal to scout, ran into several thousand rebels, and charged at once. The enemy broke; he pursued across the river and killed or captured two hundred;

sentences.zh: 收隊少二人，复衝入賊陣，奪二屍還，賊為喪氣，遂斷浮橋，焚渡船，進攻，賊望見輒靡。

translations.literal: on forming up the column two men were missing, again charged into the rebel array, recovered the two corpses and returned, the rebels lost heart, then cut the pontoon bridge, burned the ferry boats, advanced to attack, and whenever rebels saw him they were scattered.
translations.idiomatic: when he formed up, two men were missing. He charged back into the rebel lines, recovered both bodies, and returned. The rebels' morale collapsed. He cut the pontoon bridge, burned the ferry boats, pressed the attack, and wherever the rebels saw him they broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 尋克道口，复擊走桃源、輝縣援賊，合圍滑城，用地隧轟破之，文成自焚死。

translations.literal: Soon Daokou was taken, again struck and drove off relief rebels from Taoyuan and Huixian, jointly besieged Huacheng, blasted it open with a mine tunnel, and Wencheng burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took Daokou, routed relief columns from Taoyuan and Huixian, and joined the siege of Huacheng. A mine breach brought down the walls; Wencheng burned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 十二月，滑縣平，封二等男爵，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Huaxian was pacified; he was enfeoffed as second-class baron and granted the yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: By the twelfth month Huaxian had fallen. He was made a second-class baron and given the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 陝西南山賊萬五倡亂，十九年正月，移師往討，斬萬五及其黨，凡兩越月蕆事，晉一等男。

translations.literal: In southern Shaanxi the rebel Wanwu raised disturbance; in the first month of the nineteenth year he moved his army to suppress him, beheaded Wanwu and his partisans, completed the affair in two months, and was advanced to first-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: In southern Shaanxi the bandit Wanwu rose in revolt. In the first month of the nineteenth year (1814) Yuchun marched against him, killed Wanwu and his followers, and finished the campaign in two months. He was promoted to first-class baron.

sentences.zh: 陛見，仁宗慰勞有加，命至膝前，執其手曰：「朕與卿同歲，年力尚強，將來如有軍務，卿須為朕獨當一面。

translations.literal: At audience the Jiaqing Emperor comforted and praised him abundantly, ordered him before the imperial knee, took his hand and said: "I and you are the same age; our strength is still vigorous. If there is military business in the future, you must for me hold a front alone."
translations.idiomatic: At court the Jiaqing Emperor warmly praised him, called him forward, took his hand, and said, "You and I are the same age, and still strong. If war comes again, you must command a theater for me on your own."

sentences.zh: 」手賜珍物，見遇春長髯，稱美者再。

translations.literal: " He personally bestowed precious objects; seeing Yuchun's long beard, he praised it twice.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him precious gifts with his own hand. Seeing Yuchun's long beard, he praised it again and again.

sentences.zh: 時遇春弟逢春為曹州鎮總兵，命繞道視所練兵。

translations.literal: At that time Yuchun's younger brother Fengchun was commander of the Caozhou garrison; he was ordered to go by a detour to inspect the troops he had trained.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchun's younger brother Fengchun was then commander at Caozhou; the emperor told Yuchun to visit him on the way home and inspect his troops.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，加太子少保，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: When the Xuanzong Emperor ascended, he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When the Daoguang Emperor came to the throne, Yuchun was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the double-peacock-plume insignia.

sentences.zh: 道光五年，署陝甘總督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daoguang he acted as governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daoguang (1825) he served as acting governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 六年，回酋張格爾叛，詔遇春率陝、甘兵五千馳赴哈密。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Muslim chief Jahangir Khoja rebelled; an edict ordered Yuchun to lead five thousand Shaanxi and Gansu troops in rapid march to Hami.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1826) the Muslim leader Jahangir Khoja rebelled. Yuchun was ordered to rush five thousand troops from Shaanxi and Gansu to Hami.

sentences.zh: 尋命大學士長齡為揚威將軍，遇春為參贊，會兵阿克蘇進剿。

translations.literal: Soon Grand Secretary Changling was appointed Pacification Commissioner General and Yuchun commissioner; they united troops at Aksu and advanced in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Changling was soon named Pacification Commissioner General with Yuchun as his deputy. They concentrated at Aksu and marched west.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，連敗賊於洋阿爾巴特、沙布都爾、阿瓦巴特，擒斬數万，追至渾河，距喀什噶爾十餘裡，賊悉眾抗拒，列陣二十餘裡。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year he repeatedly defeated rebels at Yang'arbat, Shabudur, and Awabat, captured and killed tens of thousands, pursued to the Hun River more than ten li from Kashgar, where the rebels mustered all their forces to resist in a battle line more than twenty li long.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year (1827) he won a string of victories at Yang'arbat, Shabudur, and Awabat, killing or capturing tens of thousands. He pursued to the Hun River, a dozen li from Kashgar, where the rebels massed their entire force in a line more than twenty li long.

sentences.zh: 會大風霾，前隊迷道，未即至，將軍欲退屯十餘裡，須霽而進，遇春不可，曰：「天讚我也，賊不知我兵多少，又虞我即渡，時不可失！

translations.literal: A great wind and haze arose; the vanguard lost the road and did not arrive promptly; the general wished to withdraw and encamp more than ten li back, waiting for clearing weather to advance — Yuchun would not agree and said: "Heaven is aiding me! The rebels do not know how many troops we have, and they fear we will cross at once — the moment must not be lost!"
translations.idiomatic: A sandstorm struck. The vanguard lost its way and had not yet come up. The general wanted to fall back ten li and wait for clear weather. Yuchun refused. "Heaven is on our side," he said. "The rebels cannot tell how many men we have and fear we will cross at once. We must not miss this moment!"

sentences.zh: 且客軍利速戰，難持久。

translations.literal: Moreover guest armies profit from swift battle and cannot endure long."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, an expeditionary force needs a quick victory and cannot stay in the field long."

sentences.zh: 」乃遣千騎繞趨下游牽賊勢，自率大兵乘晦霧驟渡上游，砲聲與風沙相並，乘勢衝入賊陣，賊大奔。

translations.literal: " He then sent a thousand horsemen by a detour downstream to draw rebel strength, himself led the main force to cross suddenly upstream in the dim haze, cannon fire mingling with wind and sand, seized the momentum to charge into the rebel array, and the rebels fled in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a thousand cavalry downstream to pin the enemy, then led the main body across upstream through the murk. Cannon fire blended with the sandstorm as he drove into the rebel line; the enemy broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 三月朔，遂復喀什噶爾，甫旬日，英吉沙爾、葉爾羌、和闐以次復，加太子太保。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month Kashgar was recovered; within ten days Yengisar, Yarkand, and Khotan were recovered in succession, and he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month Kashgar was retaken. Within ten days Yengisar, Yarkand, and Khotan fell in turn. He was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 張格爾遠遁，詔遇春先入關。

translations.literal: Jahangir fled far away; an edict ordered Yuchun to enter the passes first.
translations.idiomatic: Jahangir fled into the distance. Yuchun was ordered to return through the passes ahead of the main army.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，楊芳擒張格爾於鐵蓋山，遇春入覲，捷音適至，帝大悅，賜紫韁，實授陝甘總督，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year Yang Fang captured Jahangir at Tiegai Mountain; Yuchun entered audience, timely news of victory arrived, the emperor was greatly pleased, granted the purple reins, substantively appointed him governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu, and had his portrait placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year (1828) Yang Fang captured Jahangir at Tiegai Mountain. Yuchun came to court just as word of victory arrived. The emperor was delighted, gave him the purple reins, confirmed him as governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu, and had his portrait hung in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 遇春坐鎮陝、甘凡十年，務持大體，不輕更張，討蒐軍實，鎮馭邊疆，皆有法。

translations.literal: Yuchun sat in command of Shaanxi and Gansu for ten years in all, devoted to holding the larger pattern and not lightly changing arrangements, investigated and collected military realities, and governed and restrained the frontier — all with method.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years Yuchun governed Shaanxi and Gansu, keeping to broad principles and changing little, auditing troop strength, and holding the frontier — all with settled methods.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以老予告歸，召至京，陛辭，晉封一等昭勇侯，食全俸，御製詩書扇賜之。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, on grounds of age he requested leave to retire, was summoned to the capital, took leave at audience, was advanced to first-class Marquis Zhaoyong, received full salary, and was granted a fan with an imperial poem written on it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (1835) he asked to retire on account of age, was summoned to Beijing, took his leave at court, was raised to first-class Marquis Zhaoyong with full salary, and received a fan inscribed with an imperial poem.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒於家，贈太子太傅、兵部尚書，賜金治喪，入祀賢良祠、鄉賢祠，諡忠武。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died at home; posthumously he was given Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, gold was granted for the funeral, he entered sacrifice at the Shrine of Worthies and the local worthies shrine, and his posthumous title was Zhongwu (Loyal and Martial).
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1837) he died at home. The court posthumously made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, granted funds for the funeral, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies and his home district's hall of local worthies, and gave him the posthumous name Zhongwu (Loyal and Martial).

sentences.zh: 遇春結髮從戎，大小數百戰，皆陷陣冒矢石，未嘗受毫髮傷。

translations.literal: Yuchun from the time he bound his hair entered military service; in several hundred battles large and small he always charged the lines and braved arrows and stones, yet never received the slightest wound.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yuchun had followed the colors. In hundreds of battles great and small he always led the charge under arrow and stone, yet never took so much as a scratch.

sentences.zh: 仁宗詢及，嘆為「福將」。

translations.literal: The Jiaqing Emperor inquired about this and sighed that he was a "fortunate general."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiaqing Emperor asked about it, he sighed and called him a "general blessed by fortune."

sentences.zh: 治軍善於訓練，疲卒歸部下即膽壯，或精銳改隸他人，仍不用命。

translations.literal: In governing troops he was skilled at training; weary soldiers returning to his command at once grew bold, while even elite troops transferred to others' command still would not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: He was a master trainer: worn-out soldiers grew bold again under him, while crack troops reassigned to other commanders often refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 將戰，步伐從容，雖猝遇伏，不至失措。

translations.literal: On the eve of battle his pace was unhurried; even if suddenly encountering an ambush he did not fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Before battle he moved at an unhurried pace; even a sudden ambush did not throw him off.

sentences.zh: 俘虜必入賊三月以外始誅，老稚皆赦免。

translations.literal: Captives were executed only if they had joined the rebels more than three months; the old and young were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He executed captives only if they had been with the rebels more than three months; the elderly and children were always spared.

sentences.zh: 馭降眾有恩，尤得其死力。

translations.literal: In governing surrendered masses he showed kindness and especially won their utmost devotion unto death.
translations.idiomatic: He treated surrendered rebels with kindness and won their utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 操守廉潔，治家嚴整，子弟皆謹守其家風。

translations.literal: His conduct was incorruptible, his household governance strict and orderly, and sons and younger brothers all carefully maintained his family style.
translations.idiomatic: He was incorruptible in office and strict at home; his sons and brothers all kept his family ways.

sentences.zh: 弟逢春，久隨軍中，積功授重慶鎮標游擊。

translations.literal: His younger brother Fengchun long followed in the army, accumulated merit, and was appointed regional commander of the Chongqing garrison standard.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fengchun had long served with the army, earned merit, and became regional commander of the Chongqing garrison corps.

sentences.zh: 後從賽衝阿平陝西洋縣匪，累擢山東曹州鎮總兵，調兗州鎮。

translations.literal: Later he followed Saichong'a in pacifying bandits in Yangxian, Shaanxi, was repeatedly promoted to commander of the Caozhou garrison in Shandong, and was transferred to the Yanzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He later served under Saichong'a against the Yangxian rebels in Shaanxi, rose to commander of the Caozhou garrison in Shandong, and was transferred to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 子國佐，四川茂州營都司，加副將銜。

translations.literal: His son Guozuo was commander of the Maozhou battalion in Sichuan, with the additional rank of deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guozuo served as commander of the Maozhou battalion in Sichuan and held the additional rank of deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 國楨，字海梁。

translations.literal: Guozhen, style name Hailiang.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen, whose courtesy name was Hailiang.

sentences.zh: 以舉人入貲為戶部郎中，出任潁州知府，累擢河南布政使。

translations.literal: By provincial graduate status he entered office through purchase of rank as a director in the Board of Revenue, went out as prefect of Yingzhou, and was repeatedly promoted to provincial treasurer of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he bought his way into the Board of Revenue as a director, served as prefect of Yingzhou, and rose to provincial treasurer of Henan.

sentences.zh: 洎回疆底定，宣宗推恩，就擢巡撫，疏請留其父部將訓練河南兵。

translations.literal: When the Muslim frontier was settled, the Xuanzong Emperor extended favor and promoted him directly to governor, and he memorialized to retain his father's former subordinate officers to train Henan troops.
translations.idiomatic: After the Muslim frontier was pacified, the Daoguang Emperor favored him with a direct promotion to governor. He asked to keep his father's former officers to drill the Henan troops.

sentences.zh: 武臣父子同時膺疆寄，與趙良棟、岳鍾琪兩家比盛焉。

translations.literal: A military father and son simultaneously entrusted with frontier posts — a glory comparable to the families of Zhao Liangdong and Yue Zhongqi.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son both held frontier commands at once — a distinction rivaling the houses of Zhao Liangdong and Yue Zhongqi.

sentences.zh: 遇春歿，襲侯爵，服闋，授山西巡撫，歷官皆有聲。

translations.literal: When Yuchun died, Guozhen inherited the marquisate; after mourning he was appointed governor of Shanxi, and in every post he won reputation.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuchun's death Guozhen inherited the marquisate. When mourning ended he became governor of Shanxi and earned a name in every office he held.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年，擢閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang (1841) he was made governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 尋以腿疾乞歸，在籍食俸，數年卒。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of leg ailment he begged to retire, drew salary while at home, and died after several years.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired because of a leg ailment, drew his stipend at home, and died a few years later.

sentences.zh: 遇春尤知人，獎拔如不及。

translations.literal: Yuchun was especially skilled at knowing men and rewarded and promoted as if he could not keep pace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchun had a rare gift for judging men and promoted talent as fast as he could find it.

sentences.zh: 識楊芳於卒伍中，力荐之，卒為大將，勳名與之埒，天下稱「二楊」，自有傳。

translations.literal: He recognized Yang Fang among common soldiers, strongly recommended him, and Fang in the end became a great general whose merit and fame equaled his — the realm called them the "Two Yangs," and each has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: He spotted Yang Fang in the ranks, backed him strongly, and Fang rose to become a great general of equal fame. The empire called them the "Two Yangs"; each has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 部曲多洊至專閫，著者曰吳廷剛、祝廷彪、遊棟雲。

translations.literal: Many of his subordinates in succession reached independent command; notable among them were Wu Tinggang, Zhu Tingbiao, and You Dongyun.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his officers rose in turn to independent command. The best known were Wu Tinggang, Zhu Tingbiao, and You Dongyun.

sentences.zh: 廷剛、四川成都人。

translations.literal: Tinggang was a native of Chengdu, Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggang came from Chengdu in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 由行伍徵苗，擢守備。

translations.literal: From the ranks he campaigned against the Miao and was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service in the ranks against the Miao and was promoted to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 從遇春剿教匪，善偵敵。

translations.literal: He followed Yuchun in suppressing sect rebels and was skilled at scouting the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yuchun against the White Lotus rebels and excelled at reconnaissance.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，破王登廷於青龍坪，擢都司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he defeated Wang Dengting at Qinglong Flat and was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiaqing (1799) he defeated Wang Dengting at Qinglong Flat and was made battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 五年，剿楊開甲、辛聰於龍駒寨，倍道掩襲，敗賊輝塔、洞寨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he suppressed Yang Kaijia and Xin Cong at Longju stockade, made a forced march by hidden route for a surprise attack, and defeated rebels at Huita and Dong stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he fought Yang Kaijia and Xin Cong at Longju stockade, made a night march by a hidden path, and routed the rebels at Huita and Dong stockades.

sentences.zh: 伍金柱踞手板岩，輕騎往探，獲賊諜，馳報，得大捷。

translations.literal: Wu Jinzhu held Shouban Rock; Tinggang went with light cavalry to reconnoiter, captured a rebel spy, rode back to report, and a great victory was won.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Jinzhu held Shouban Rock, Tinggang rode out lightly to scout, seized a rebel spy, reported at once, and helped win a great victory.

sentences.zh: 追張天倫至馬桑壩，高天升、戴仕傑由箭桿山突出，迎擊，大敗之，擢游擊。

translations.literal: Pursuing Zhang Tianlun to Masangba, Gao Tiansheng and Dai Shijie burst out from Jiangan Mountain; he met and struck them and routed them greatly, and was promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing Zhang Tianlun to Masangba, he met Gao Tiansheng and Dai Shijie bursting from Jiangan Mountain, defeated them soundly, and was promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 六年，孫家坡之戰，分追餘賊至關埡，奪據山頂，賊多墜崖死，擢參將。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, at the battle of Sunjiapo, he split off in pursuit of remnant rebels to Guanya, seized the hilltop, and many rebels fell from cliffs to their deaths; he was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Sunjiapo in the sixth year he pursued stragglers to Guanya, seized the hilltop, and drove many rebels over the cliffs to their deaths. He was promoted to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 追高見奇、姚馨佐至通江，山徑紆險，棄馬行，見賊數十人，奪路走，擒其酋，乃辛鬥也。

translations.literal: Pursuing Gao Jianqi and Yao Xinzu to Tongjiang on winding perilous mountain paths, he abandoned his horse and went on foot, saw several dozen rebels, seized the road and fled, and captured their chief — it was Xin Dou.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing Gao Jianqi and Yao Xinzu into Tongjiang on narrow mountain tracks, he left his horse and went on foot, saw a few dozen rebels, cut off their escape, and took their chief Xin Dou.

sentences.zh: 通江賊李彬夜竄熊家灣，廷剛先至，橫衝賊為二，後賊回竄，與大軍夾擊，大破之，擒魏中均、苟朝萬、王士元。

translations.literal: Tongjiang rebel Li Bin fled by night to Xiongjiawan; Tinggang arrived first, cut the rebels in two, then when rear rebels turned back he joined the main army in a pincer and won a great victory, capturing Wei Zhongjun, Gou Chaowan, and Wang Shiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bin of Tongjiang fled by night to Xiongjiawan, Tinggang got there first, split the rebel column, and when the rear guard turned back he and the main force crushed them, taking Wei Zhongjun, Gou Chaowan, and Wang Shiyuan.

sentences.zh: 七年，迭擊辛聰、劉永受於老君嶺、菜子坪、太平峒、燕子岩，賊四竄；

translations.literal: In the seventh year he repeatedly struck Xin Cong and Liu Yongshou at Laojun Ridge, Caiziping, Taiping cave, and Yanziyan, and the rebels scattered in four directions;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he repeatedly attacked Xin Cong and Liu Yongshou at Laojun Ridge, Caiziping, Taiping cave, and Yanziyan until the rebels broke four ways;

sentences.zh: 偕祝廷彪徒步入山，追賊田峪，將歸隊，過桃川沙壩，見山樹紅旗，疑之，偵知賊首苟文明冒官軍，奮擊敗之，分路要截，擒斬數百。

translations.literal: with Zhu Tingbiao he entered the mountains on foot, pursued rebels to Tianyu, was returning to his unit when passing Taoyuan Shaba he saw red banners in the trees, suspected them, learned by reconnaissance that rebel chief Gou Wenming was impersonating government troops, fought fiercely and defeated them, blocked by separate routes, and captured or killed several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: with Zhu Tingbiao he marched on foot into the hills, chased rebels to Tianyu, and on the way back past Taoyuan Shaba saw red flags in the trees. Scouts revealed Gou Wenming posing as imperial troops. He attacked, won, and cut off their retreat, killing or capturing hundreds.

sentences.zh: 文明將入川，追至花石岩，見山上炊煙起，麾兵仰攻，文明知不能脫，擲跳岩下，就斬之；

translations.literal: Wenming was about to enter Sichuan; he pursued to Huashiyan, saw cooking smoke rising on the hill, waved his troops to attack uphill; Wenming knew he could not escape, threw himself from the cliff, and was beheaded where he fell;
translations.idiomatic: Wenming tried to slip into Sichuan. Tinggang chased him to Huashiyan, saw smoke on the heights, and ordered an uphill assault. Wenming, seeing no escape, leaped from the cliff and was beheaded on the spot;

sentences.zh: 又擒殲苟七麻子、吳廷詔、張芳等。

translations.literal: again captured and annihilated Gou Qimazi, Wu Tingzhao, Zhang Fang, and others.
translations.idiomatic: he also killed or captured Gou Qimazi, Wu Tingzhao, Zhang Fang, and others.

sentences.zh: 八年，搜剿南山餘匪，往來老林。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he searched out and suppressed remnant rebels in the southern hills, going back and forth in the old forests.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he hunted down southern hill rebels, ranging through the deep old forests.

sentences.zh: 九年，賊聚川、陝邊界，廷剛至桃木坪，賊乘霧衝撲，受矛傷，窮追越楚境，迭敗之石渣河、亢喜坡。

translations.literal: In the ninth year rebels gathered on the Sichuan-Shaanxi border; Tinggang reached Taomuping, rebels charged through the fog, he was wounded by a spear, pursued in desperation across the Chu border, and repeatedly defeated them at Shizha River and Kangxipo.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year rebels massed on the Sichuan-Shaanxi border. At Taomuping they rushed him through the mist and wounded him with a spear, but he chased them across the Hubei border and beat them at Shizha River and Kangxipo.

sentences.zh: 進攻馬鞍山，賊伏陡崖，徑馳上，擒賈燦華、苟文華、王振、謝尚玉等。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Ma'an Mountain, rebels lay in ambush on a steep cliff; he charged straight up the path and captured Jia Canhua, Gou Wenhua, Wang Zhen, Xie Shangyu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: At Ma'an Mountain rebels hid on a steep cliff. He rode straight up and took Jia Canhua, Gou Wenhua, Wang Zhen, Xie Shangyu, and others.

sentences.zh: 賊遁老山，偕祝廷彪選健卒持乾崿輕騎躡剿，遍歷險僻。

translations.literal: Rebels fled to the old mountains; with Zhu Tingbiao he chose hardy troops with dry rations and light cavalry to pursue and suppress, traversing every perilous and remote place.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled into the deep mountains. With Zhu Tingbiao he picked hardy men with dry rations and light cavalry and scoured every remote defile.

sentences.zh: 至十年，擒斬殆盡，擢甘肅涼州鎮總兵，調漢中鎮。

translations.literal: By the tenth year they were nearly all captured or killed; he was promoted to commander of the Liangzhou garrison in Gansu and transferred to the Hanzhong garrison.
translations.idiomatic: By the tenth year the rebels were nearly wiped out. He was made commander at Liangzhou in Gansu and transferred to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 十八年，剿三才峽匪萬五，別賊起古子溝，分兵克之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he suppressed the Sancai Gorge bandit Wanwu; other rebels rose at Guzigou and he detached troops to take them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1813) he suppressed Wanwu at Sancai Gorge; when rebels rose at Guzigou he sent a detachment to crush them.

sentences.zh: 萬五乘間連踞峒寨，敗之於袁家莊、平木山梁，分兵抄襲，設伏沙壩，擒其黨週在庭、週之順。

translations.literal: Wanwu seized the chance to hold successive cave stockades; Tinggang defeated him at Yuanjiazhuang and Pingmushanliang, detached troops for a flanking strike, and set an ambush at Shaba, capturing his partisans Zhou Zaiting and Zhou Zhishun.
translations.idiomatic: Wanwu seized one cave stockade after another. Tinggang beat him at Yuanjiazhuang and Pingmushanliang, flanked him with a detached column, and ambushed his men at Shaba, taking Zhou Zaiting and Zhou Zhishun.

sentences.zh: 萬五窮蹙，竄盩厔山中，為他軍所擒。

translations.literal: Wanwu, driven to extremity, fled into the Zhounan mountains and was captured by another army.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Wanwu fled into the Zhounan mountains and was taken by another column.

sentences.zh: 進剿餘黨，擒尹朝貴、劉功。

translations.literal: Advancing to suppress remnant partisans, he captured Yin Chaogui and Liu Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He then hunted down the survivors and captured Yin Chaogui and Liu Gong.

sentences.zh: 十九年，事平，詔廷剛首先進剿，功最，加提督銜。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, when the affair was settled, an edict said Tinggang had led the first advance in suppression and his merit ranked foremost; he was given the additional rank of commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year (1814), when the campaign ended, an edict praised Tinggang for leading the first assault and ranking first in merit. He received the additional rank of commander.

sentences.zh: 尋擢廣東陸路提督，未至，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to land forces commander of Guangdong but died before he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to land forces commander of Guangdong but died before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 詔念前勞，予優恤，諡壯勤。

translations.literal: An edict recalled his former labors, granted favorable condolence payments, and gave the posthumous title Zhuangqin (Stalwart and Diligent).
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled his long service, granted generous mourning benefits, and gave him the posthumous name Zhuangqin (Stalwart and Diligent).

sentences.zh: 廷彪，四川雙流人。

translations.literal: Tingbiao was a native of Shuangliu, Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tingbiao came from Shuangliu in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 由行伍徵苗，擢守備。

translations.literal: From the ranks he campaigned against the Miao and was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the ranks against the Miao and rose to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，從遇春殲劉元恭、劉開玉，擢都司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing he followed Yuchun in annihilating Liu Yungong and Liu Kaiyu and was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiaqing he followed Yuchun in wiping out Liu Yungong and Liu Kaiyu and was made battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 六年，擒王廷詔，擢游擊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he captured Wang Tingzhao and was promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he captured Wang Tingzhao and was promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 七年，勦賊平安寨，設伏長溝，乘夜掩擊，中矛傷，裹創力戰，斃苟文清於陣；

translations.literal: In the seventh year he suppressed rebels at Ping'an stockade, set an ambush at Longgou, made a night surprise attack, was wounded by a spear, fought on with bandaged wounds, and killed Gou Wenqing in the battle line;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he stormed Ping'an stockade, laid an ambush at Longgou, attacked by night, took a spear wound, fought on with bandaged wounds, and killed Gou Wenqing in the melee;

sentences.zh: 偕吳廷剛殲苟文明於花石岩，擒苟文齊於鱉鍋山：擢參將。

translations.literal: with Wu Tinggang he annihilated Gou Wenming at Huashiyan and captured Gou Wenqi at Bieguoshan: he was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: with Wu Tinggang he destroyed Gou Wenming at Huashiyan and took Gou Wenqi at Bieguoshan. He was promoted to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 又破張世云於北溝口。

translations.literal: Again he defeated Zhang Shiyun at Beigoukou.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated Zhang Shiyun at Beigoukou.

sentences.zh: 八年，迭擊賊於老林、小岔溝、白果園，擒冉璠。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he repeatedly struck rebels in the old forest, Xiaochagou, and Baiguoyuan and captured Ran Fan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he repeatedly attacked rebels in the old forest, Xiaochagou, and Baiguoyuan and captured Ran Fan.

sentences.zh: 九年，偕羅思舉追賊入界嶺老林，攻望都觀賊巢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, with Luo Siju, he pursued rebels into the Jieling old forest and attacked the rebel nest at Wangdu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, with Luo Siju, he chased rebels into the Jieling old forest and stormed their nest at Wangdu Temple.

sentences.zh: 從遇春擊賊鳳凰寨、壩口、馬鞍山，並多斬獲。

translations.literal: He followed Yuchun in striking rebels at Fenghuang stockade, Bakou, and Ma'an Mountain, with many captures and kills in each.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yuchun against rebels at Fenghuang stockade, Bakou, and Ma'an Mountain and took many heads in each fight.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢漢中協副將。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to deputy commander of the Hanzhong garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was made deputy commander of the Hanzhong garrison.

sentences.zh: 值寧陝兵變，赴南山截剿。

translations.literal: When the Ningshan garrison mutinied, he went to the southern hills to intercept and suppress.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ningshan garrison mutinied, he marched to the southern hills to cut them off.

sentences.zh: 甫定，瓦石坪周士貴復起，偕羅思舉合擊擒之，賜號迅勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Just as that was settled, Zhou Shigui of Washiping rose again; with Luo Siju he jointly attacked and captured him, and was granted the title Swift Brave Batu.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly was that over when Zhou Shigui of Washiping rebelled again. With Luo Siju he attacked and captured him and received the title Swift Brave Batu.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢甘肅寧夏鎮總兵，調陝西西安鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to commander of the Ningxia garrison in Gansu and transferred to the Xi'an garrison in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became commander at Ningxia in Gansu and was transferred to Xi'an in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 十九年，剿三才峽匪萬五餘黨，偕吳廷剛擒尹朝貴於木瓜園。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he suppressed remnant partisans of Wanwu at Sancai Gorge and with Wu Tinggang captured Yin Chaogui at Mugua Garden.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he hunted Wanwu's remnants at Sancai Gorge and with Wu Tinggang captured Yin Chaogui at Mugua Garden.

sentences.zh: 分路勦賊黃草坪，毀其巢，追入手板岩老林，賊詭降，設伏，擒其渠陳四，擢湖南提督。

translations.literal: He split forces to suppress rebels at Huangcaoping, destroyed their nest, pursued into the Shouban Rock old forest; the rebels feigned surrender and set an ambush — he captured their leader Chen Si and was promoted to commander of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He detached troops against Huangcaoping, burned their nest, and pursued into the Shouban Rock forest. When the rebels pretended to surrender and ambushed him, he seized their chief Chen Si and was made commander of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光三年，內召，授頭等侍衛，仍兼提督銜。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang he was summoned to court, appointed first-class imperial bodyguard, while still holding the additional rank of commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daoguang (1823) he was called to court as a first-class imperial bodyguard while retaining his commander rank.

sentences.zh: 以熟悉南山情形，未幾，复授西安鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Because he knew the southern hills well, before long he was again appointed commander of the Xi'an garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the southern hills well, he was soon back as commander at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 在任凡十年，擢貴州提督，調浙江提督。

translations.literal: In office ten years in all, he was promoted to commander of Guizhou and transferred to commander of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years in post he was promoted to Guizhou and then transferred to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 二十年，英吉利兵陷定海，守招​​寶山，吏議褫職，詔留任。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when English troops took Dinghai, he defended Zhaobao Mountain; the civil officials proposed dismissal, but an edict ordered him retained.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (1840), when British forces took Dinghai, he defended Zhaobao Mountain. Officials urged his removal, but the throne kept him in place.

sentences.zh: 尋以年老休致，歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Soon, on grounds of age he retired, returned home, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired on account of age, went home, and died there.

sentences.zh: 廷彪果敢力戰，善撫士卒，當時降眾多生事，所部帖然，世稱之。

translations.literal: Tingbiao was bold and decisive in battle, skilled at comforting troops; at the time surrendered masses often caused trouble, but his command was orderly — contemporaries praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Tingbiao fought boldly and knew how to win soldiers' hearts. When surrendered rebels often made trouble elsewhere, his men stayed quiet — a quality men praised at the time.

sentences.zh: 棟雲，四川巫山人，寄籍華陽。

translations.literal: Dongyun was a native of Wushan, Sichuan, with registered domicile at Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: Dongyun was from Wushan in Sichuan but registered his domicile at Huayang.

sentences.zh: 以武舉補把總，從征廓爾喀、苗疆，積功累擢寧羌營游擊。

translations.literal: By military examination he was made platoon leader; he campaigned against Gurkha and the Miao frontier, accumulated merit, and was repeatedly promoted to regional commander of the Ningqiang battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Through the military examination he became a platoon leader, fought in Gurkha and on the Miao frontier, and rose to regional commander of the Ningqiang battalion.

sentences.zh: 從額勒登保剿教匪，與遇春偕，後乃為其部將。

translations.literal: He followed Ereldunbao in suppressing sect rebels together with Yuchun, and afterward became his subordinate officer.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Ereldunbao against the White Lotus rebels alongside Yuchun and later became one of Yuchun's officers.

sentences.zh: 攻終報寨先登，功最。

translations.literal: In assaulting Zhongbao stockade he was first to scale the wall; his merit ranked foremost.
translations.idiomatic: He was first over the wall at Zhongbao stockade and topped the merit rolls.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，從遇春追張漢潮、詹世爵、李槐等，由漢中入川境。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing he followed Yuchun in pursuing Zhang Hanchao, Zhan Shijue, and Li Huai, entering Sichuan territory from Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiaqing he followed Yuchun in chasing Zhang Hanchao, Zhan Shijue, and Li Huai from Hanzhong into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 諸軍合剿於隘口，棟雲據高俯擊，斷槐手，箭貫世爵胸，皆斃。

translations.literal: The various armies jointly suppressed at the pass; Dongyun held the heights and struck downward, severed Huai's hand, and an arrow pierced Shijue's chest — both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: At the pass the columns converged. Dongyun held the high ground, struck downward, cut off Li Huai's hand, and put an arrow through Zhan Shijue's chest — both died.

sentences.zh: 漢潮竄梅子關，迎擊，敗之；

translations.literal: Hanchao fled to Meizi Pass; Dongyun met and struck him and defeated him;
translations.idiomatic: Hanchao fled to Meizi Pass; Dongyun intercepted and routed him;

sentences.zh: 又連敗之巴東及陝境兩河關。

translations.literal: again repeatedly defeated him at Badong and at Lianghe Pass on the Shaanxi border.
translations.idiomatic: then beat him again at Badong and at Lianghe Pass on the Shaanxi frontier.

sentences.zh: 設伏王家河，賊至，痛殲之，窮追至河南盧氏，漢潮遁。

translations.literal: He set an ambush at Wangjia River; when rebels came he annihilated them severely, pursued in desperation to Lushi in Henan, and Hanchao escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He ambushed them at Wangjia River, destroyed them, and chased them to Lushi in Henan before Hanchao slipped away.

sentences.zh: 四年春，敗賊涼沁河，兵僅五百，斬獲三百餘級。

translations.literal: In spring of the fourth year he defeated rebels at Liangqin River with only five hundred troops and killed or captured more than three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year he beat rebels at Liangqin River with only five hundred men and killed or captured more than three hundred.

sentences.zh: 賊走龍駒寨，屯康家河，棟雲躡之，忽山坳突出悍賊，中矛傷，戰愈力，射殪執旗者，賊乃卻。

translations.literal: Rebels fled to Longju stockade and encamped at Kangjia River; Dongyun pursued them when suddenly fierce rebels burst from a mountain hollow; he was wounded by a spear, fought all the harder, shot dead the banner bearer, and the rebels retreated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to Longju stockade and camped at Kangjia River. As Dongyun closed in, fierce rebels burst from a ravine. He took a spear wound but fought harder, shot the standard bearer, and the enemy fell back.

sentences.zh: 事聞，特詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, a special edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The court heard of it and issued a special edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 四月，漢潮踞紅門寺，冒雨出間道擊走之，扼之黑龍口，與明亮、興肇為犄角。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Hanchao held Hongmen Temple; Dongyun marched through rain by a hidden path, struck and drove him off, blocked him at Heilong Pass, and with Mingliang and Xingzhao formed a pincer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Hanchao held Hongmen Temple. Dongyun came through rain on a hidden track, drove him off, and with Mingliang and Xingzhao penned him at Heilong Pass.

sentences.zh: 谿水漲，潛涉上游襲擊，賊大潰，又冒雨克欒家河。

translations.literal: The stream rose; he secretly crossed upstream to strike, the rebels fled in great disorder, and again in the rain he took Luanjia River.
translations.idiomatic: When the stream rose he waded upstream under cover and struck; the rebels broke. In the rain he then took Luanjia River.

sentences.zh: 八月，敗賊犁澤坪，竄石峽子，棟雲設伏野雞溝，與大兵夾擊，漢潮窮蹙入老林；

translations.literal: In the eighth month he defeated rebels at Lize Flat; they fled to Shixiazi; Dongyun set an ambush at Yejigou and with the main army struck in concert; Hanchao, driven to extremity, entered the old forest;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he routed rebels at Lize Flat. They fled to Shixiazi; he ambushed them at Yejigou and, with the main force, drove Hanchao into the deep forest;

sentences.zh: 分路追剿，擒李潮於張家坪，而漢潮已為明亮擊斃，至是獲其屍：擢甘肅提標參將。

translations.literal: splitting forces in pursuit and suppression, he captured Li Chao at Zhangjiaping, while Hanchao had already been killed by Mingliang — when his corpse was obtained it was thus confirmed: he was promoted to deputy commander of the Gansu commander's standard.
translations.idiomatic: he split his men in pursuit, captured Li Chao at Zhangjiaping, and confirmed that Mingliang had already killed Hanchao. He was promoted to deputy commander of the Gansu commander's standard.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢安慶協副將。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to deputy commander of the Anqing garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made deputy commander of the Anqing garrison.

sentences.zh: 敗冉學勝於沔陽，連擊高天德、馬學禮於獅子梁、櫻桃埡；

translations.literal: He defeated Ran Xuesheng at Mianyang and repeatedly struck Gao Tiande and Ma Xueli at Shiziliang and Yingtao'ya;
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Ran Xuesheng at Mianyang and repeatedly attacked Gao Tiande and Ma Xueli at Shiziliang and Yingtao'ya;

sentences.zh: 六年春，复破之於五郎坪、鳳凰山。

translations.literal: in spring of the sixth year he again defeated them at Wulangping and Fenghuang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: in the spring of the sixth year he beat them again at Wulangping and Fenghuang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 天德、學禮為遇春所擒。

translations.literal: Tiande and Xueli were captured by Yuchun.
translations.idiomatic: Tiande and Xueli were taken by Yuchun.

sentences.zh: 餘黨踞八斗坪，棟雲分隊襲之，擒羅鳳友；

translations.literal: Remnant partisans held Badouping; Dongyun detached a unit to strike them and captured Luo Fengyou;
translations.idiomatic: Remnants held Badouping; Dongyun sent a detachment, stormed them, and captured Luo Fengyou;

sentences.zh: 又破伍金柱餘黨於三岔坪。

translations.literal: again he defeated Wu Jinzhu's remnant partisans at Sanchaping.
translations.idiomatic: he also broke Wu Jinzhu's survivors at Sanchaping.

sentences.zh: 至七年春，所部凱撤，擢狼山鎮總兵，父憂去官。

translations.literal: By spring of the seventh year his unit withdrew in victory; he was promoted to commander of the Langshan garrison and left office on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: By the spring of the seventh year his troops marched home in triumph. He was made commander at Langshan and left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授河州鎮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed to the Hezhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was given the Hezhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 西寧番族出擾，​​棟雲專剿貴德一路，破賊甘壩山，連敗之六哈圖河、什尖裡、斡汪科合山，遂克沙卜浪賊巢，進至紅露井。

translations.literal: Tibetan tribes of Xining came out to raid; Dongyun solely suppressed the Guide route, defeated rebels at Ganbashan, repeatedly defeated them at Liuhatu River, Shijianli, and Wangwangkehe Mountain, then took the Shabulang rebel nest and advanced to Honglujing.
translations.idiomatic: When Xining Tibetans raided, Dongyun cleared the Guide route alone, beat them at Ganbashan, won again at Liuhatu River, Shijianli, and Wangwangkehe Mountain, stormed Shabulang, and advanced to Honglujing.

sentences.zh: 番僧昂賢率十二族降，焚其巢，番境悉平。

translations.literal: The Tibetan monk Angxian led twelve tribes to surrender; their nests were burned and the Tibetan frontier was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Angxian brought twelve tribes to surrender. Their camps were burned and the Tibetan border was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去，起補陝安鎮，調寧夏鎮。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's death, was recalled to fill the post at Shaan'an garrison, and was transferred to the Ningxia garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He left to mourn his mother, was recalled to Shaan'an, and was transferred to Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 十八年，從遇春剿南山匪，數戰於隴州、沔陽，擒賊渠。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he followed Yuchun in suppressing southern hill bandits, fought several battles in Longzhou and Mianyang, and captured rebel chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he followed Yuchun against the southern hill rebels, fought several times in Longzhou and Mianyang, and took rebel chiefs.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，標弁江芝誣訐棟雲侵餉，下總督察治，得白，抵芝罪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year a standard-bearer Jiang Zhi falsely accused Dongyun of embezzling rations; the commander investigated and he was cleared, while Zhi was punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year a sergeant named Jiang Zhi falsely accused Dongyun of stealing rations. The commander investigated, cleared him, and punished Zhi.

sentences.zh: 棟雲坐私役兵丁，褫職，詔赴遇春軍委用。

translations.literal: Dongyun was punished for privately employing soldiers, stripped of rank, and ordered to go to Yuchun's army for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Dongyun was found to have used troops for private labor, lost his rank, and was ordered to serve under Yuchun.

sentences.zh: 道光初，署鹽茶都司，乞病歸，卒。

translations.literal: In early Daoguang he acted as salt-tea director, begged leave on grounds of illness, returned home, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daoguang he served as salt-tea director, retired sick, went home, and died.

sentences.zh: 羅思舉，字天鵬，四川東鄉人。

translations.literal: Luo Siju, style name Tianpeng, was a native of Dongxiang, Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Siju, courtesy name Tianpeng, came from Dongxiang in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 少有膽略，蹻捷，逾屋如飛。

translations.literal: In youth he had courage and resourcefulness, was nimble and agile, leaping over roofs like flight.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bold and quick, leaping over rooftops like a bird.

sentences.zh: 貧困，為盜秦、豫、川、楚間。

translations.literal: In poverty he became a bandit between Qin, Yu, Chuan, and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and desperate, he turned bandit across Shaanxi, Henan, Sichuan, and Hubei.

sentences.zh: 結客報仇，數殺不義者。

translations.literal: He gathered companions to avenge wrongs and several times killed the unrighteous.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered sworn brothers to settle scores and killed several men he judged wicked.

sentences.zh: 遭阨，幸不死，久之自​​悔。

translations.literal: He met disaster but fortunately did not die; after long years he came to regret it himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was nearly killed more than once but survived; in time he repented.

sentences.zh: 教匪起，充鄉勇，誓殺賊立功名。

translations.literal: When sect rebels rose he joined the local militia, vowing to kill rebels and win fame.
translations.idiomatic: When the White Lotus rebels rose he joined the militia, swearing to kill rebels and win honor.

sentences.zh: 王三槐踞東鄉豐城為巢，眾數万，官軍莫敢擊，出掠羅家壩，團勇不習戰。

translations.literal: Wang Sanhuai held Fengcheng in Dongxiang as his nest with tens of thousands; government troops dared not attack; he went out to raid Luojiaba while the militia were unskilled in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sanhuai held Dongxiang's Fengcheng with tens of thousands of men. Government troops dared not attack. When he raided Luojiaba the militia were raw recruits.

sentences.zh: 思舉見賊前鋒數百，詭呼曰：「數十人耳！

translations.literal: Siju saw several hundred rebel vanguard troops and cried deceitfully: "Only several tens of men!"
translations.idiomatic: Siju saw a few hundred rebel vanguard and shouted falsely, "Only a few dozen men!"

sentences.zh: 」眾氣倍，擊走之。

translations.literal: " The men's spirit doubled, and they struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: The militia took heart and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 游擊羅定國使偵豐城，還報：「請率死士夜搗之，官兵外應，可一舉滅。

translations.literal: Regional commander Luo Dingguo sent him to scout Fengcheng; on return he reported: "Please let me lead dare-to-die men by night to storm it; government troops respond from outside and it can be destroyed in one stroke."
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Luo Dingguo sent him to scout Fengcheng. He reported, "Give me volunteers to storm it by night while the regulars strike from outside, and we can wipe them out at once."

sentences.zh: 」定國以為狂。

translations.literal: Dingguo thought him mad.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo thought him reckless.

sentences.zh: 思舉憤，獨攜火藥往，乘烈風燔之。

translations.literal: Siju in anger went alone carrying gunpowder, and riding a fierce wind burned the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Siju went alone with gunpowder and, when a strong wind rose, set the camp ablaze.

sentences.zh: 賊黑夜相蹂殺，走巔岩，踣死無算，遂奔南壩場。

translations.literal: The rebels in the dark night slaughtered one another, fled to the cliff tops, and countless fell to their deaths; they then fled to Nanbaba.
translations.idiomatic: In the dark the rebels turned on one another, fled to the cliffs, and countless fell to their deaths before fleeing to Nanbacha.

sentences.zh: 是役，一夫走賊數万，聲震川東，總督英善給七品軍功，隸副都統佛住。

translations.literal: In this campaign one man routed tens of thousands of rebels; his fame shook eastern Sichuan. Governor Yingshan granted him seventh-rank military merit and placed him under the deputy commandant Fozhu.
translations.idiomatic: One man had routed tens of thousands of rebels; his name shook eastern Sichuan. Governor Yingshan gave him seventh-rank military merit and attached him to Deputy Commandant Fozhu.

sentences.zh: 川賊以羅其清、冉文儔、徐天德、王三槐為最強，徐、王二賊合窺東鄉。

translations.literal: Among Sichuan rebels Luo Qiqing, Ran Wenchou, Xu Tiande, and Wang Sanhuai were strongest; Xu and Wang joined forces to watch Dongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The strongest Sichuan rebels were Luo Qiqing, Ran Wenchou, Xu Tiande, and Wang Sanhuai. Xu and Wang joined to threaten Dongxiang.

sentences.zh: 思舉請佛住嚴備，勿聽。

translations.literal: Siju asked Fozhu to make strict preparations; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Siju urged Fozhu to prepare defenses, but Fozhu refused.

sentences.zh: 乃為知縣劉清說其清降，知其詐，馳歸，則賊已陷東鄉，戕佛住，清亦拔營去。

translations.literal: He then persuaded Magistrate Liu Qing to induce Qiqing to surrender, knew it was a trick, and rode back — but the rebels had already taken Dongxiang, killed Fozhu, and Qing had also withdrawn his camp.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to persuade Magistrate Liu Qing to lure Luo Qiqing into surrender, saw through the ruse, and rode back — only to find Dongxiang fallen, Fozhu killed, and Qing's camp gone.

sentences.zh: 時嘉慶二年正月也。

translations.literal: It was the first month of the second year of Jiaqing.
translations.idiomatic: This was the first month of the second year of Jiaqing (1797).

sentences.zh: 調苗疆凱旋兵猶未至，總兵索費音阿率甘肅兵來援，用思舉策，紮營大團堡，開壕樹柵，埋火藥，誘賊入，轟之，遂奪金峨寺賊巢，復東鄉。

translations.literal: Troops returning victorious from the Miao frontier had not yet arrived; Commander Suofeiyin'a led Gansu troops to relieve them, used Siju's plan, encamped at Datuanbao, dug trenches and set palisades, buried gunpowder, lured rebels in and blasted them, then retook the Jin'e Temple rebel nest and recovered Dongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Victorious Miao troops had not yet returned when Commander Suofeiyin'a brought Gansu reinforcements. Using Siju's plan they camped at Datuanbao, dug trenches, buried powder, lured the rebels in and blew them up, retook the Jin'e Temple nest, and recovered Dongxiang.

sentences.zh: 賊竄重石子、香爐坪，德楞泰、明亮並以兵會，思舉請仍如破豐城事，德楞泰壯之。

translations.literal: Rebels fled to Chongshizi and Xiangluping; Delengtai and Mingliang both joined with troops; Siju asked to repeat the Fengcheng stratagem and Delengtai praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to Chongshizi and Xiangluping. Delengtai and Mingliang converged with their columns. Siju asked to repeat the Fengcheng trick, and Delengtai approved.

sentences.zh: 隻身夜入賊營，會大雨，火藥不燃，賊覺，懼而遁。
