translations.literal: Alone at night he entered the rebel camp; heavy rain came and the powder would not ignite; the rebels noticed and fled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the rebel camp alone at night, but rain soaked the powder. The rebels discovered him and fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 自是常將鄉勇，分路為奇兵，與官軍犄角，或為前鋒，殲孫士鳳於淨土庵，又敗賊於峨城山，皆以火攻劫營獲捷。

translations.literal: From then on he often led militia on separate routes as irregular troops in pincer with government forces, or as vanguard, annihilated Sun Shifeng at Jingtu'an, again defeated rebels at Echeng Mountain — all victories won by fire attack and raiding camps.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he often led militia as skirmishers in concert with regular troops — sometimes as vanguard — killing Sun Shifeng at Jingtu'an and beating rebels at Echeng Mountain, always by fire and night raids.

sentences.zh: 時川賊與襄陽賊齊王氏等合，雲陽教黨亦起應。

translations.literal: At the time Sichuan rebels joined with Xiangyang rebels such as the Wang clan; Yunyang sect partisans also rose in response.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan rebels had joined the Xiangyang rebels under the Wangs, and Yunyang sect followers rose in support.

sentences.zh: 獲諜，知王三槐將赴陳家山，即假所獲賊旗，夜馳往，聲言白號賊至，賊下山迎，悉誘殲之，擒賊首高名貴，其黨張長庚覺而奔，追斬甚眾，擢千總。

translations.literal: He obtained a spy and learned Wang Sanhuai would go to Chenjiashan; he at once used captured rebel banners, rode by night, and cried that White Banner rebels had come; rebels came down the hill to welcome them and were all lured in and annihilated; rebel chief Gao Minggui was captured; partisan Zhang Changgeng noticed and fled — many were pursued and killed; he was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: A spy told him Wang Sanhuai would visit Chenjiashan. Siju took captured rebel flags, rode by night, and announced that White Banner rebels had arrived. The rebels came down to greet them and were wiped out. He took the chief Gao Minggui; Zhang Changgeng escaped but many were cut down on the chase. He was made company commander.

sentences.zh: 三年，總督勒保誘擒三槐，其黨冷天祿踞安樂坪，環攻不下；

translations.literal: In the third year Governor Lebao lured and captured Sanhuai; his partisan Leng Tianlu held Anleping and could not be taken by encirclement;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Governor Lebao captured Sanhuai by ruse. His lieutenant Leng Tianlu held Anleping and resisted siege;

sentences.zh: 召思舉往，夜率死士焚其巢。

translations.literal: Siju was summoned; at night he led dare-to-die men and burned their nest.
translations.idiomatic: Siju was called in and at night led volunteers to burn the nest.

sentences.zh: 將明，殿旅出，大呼曰：「我豐城劫寨羅思舉也！

translations.literal: As dawn neared the main column came out; he cried loudly: "I am Luo Siju who raided Fengcheng stockade!"
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the main column advanced. He shouted, "I am Luo Siju of the Fengcheng raid!"

sentences.zh: 」賊膽落，潰圍走。

translations.literal: " The rebels' courage collapsed and they broke the encirclement and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels lost heart and broke out of the siege.

sentences.zh: 思舉戰績至是始上聞，擢守備。

translations.literal: Siju's battle achievements only now reached the court; he was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Only now did Siju's exploits reach the capital. He was promoted to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 德楞泰圍羅其清等於箕山，復召思舉問計。

translations.literal: Delengtai besieged Luo Qiqing and others at Jishan and again summoned Siju to ask his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Delengtai besieged Luo Qiqing at Jishan and again asked Siju's counsel.

sentences.zh: 思舉相地勢，曰：「賊各隘皆壘石守，惟山後懸削數十丈，必恃險乏備。

translations.literal: Siju surveyed the terrain and said: "Every rebel pass is blocked with piled stones, but the rear of the mountain hangs sheer for several tens of zhang — they must rely on peril and be poorly guarded."
translations.idiomatic: Surveying the ground he said, "Every pass is blocked with stone, but the rear cliff drops sheer for dozens of zhang. They trust the terrain and leave it thinly held."

sentences.zh: 若官軍攻於前，使不暇他顧；

translations.literal: If government troops attack in front so they have no leisure for other concerns;
translations.idiomatic: If the regulars attack in front and hold their attention;

sentences.zh: 我率勇敢者梯而上，可搗也。

translations.literal: I will lead the brave up by scaling ladders and can storm them."
translations.idiomatic: I will take the brave up the cliff and storm them from behind."

sentences.zh: 」如其言，夾擊，大破之，餘賊四逸。

translations.literal: " As he said, they struck from both sides and won a great victory; remnant rebels scattered in four directions.
translations.idiomatic: It worked. The pincer broke them; the survivors scattered four ways.

sentences.zh: 思舉料其必走方山坪，率鄉勇先往，伏坪後，越數日，賊為官軍追擊，果至，擒斬幾盡，遂獲其清。

translations.literal: Siju judged they would surely flee to Fangshanping, led militia ahead, lay in ambush behind the flat; after several days rebels pursued by government troops came as expected; nearly all were captured or killed, and Qiqing was thus taken.
translations.idiomatic: He expected them to flee to Fangshanping, led militia there first, and hid behind the flat. Days later the pursued rebels came as he foretold; nearly all were killed or taken, and Qiqing was captured.

sentences.zh: 四年，其清餘黨踞東鄉四季坪，從提督七十五破之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Qiqing's remnant partisans held Sijiping in Dongxiang; he followed Commander Qishiwu in breaking them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Qiqing's remnants held Sijiping in Dongxiang; he followed Commander Qishiwu and broke them.

sentences.zh: 秋，敗賊巴州豆真坡，又援田朝貴於鐵爐山。

translations.literal: In autumn he defeated rebels at Douzhenpo in Bazhou and again relieved Tian Chaogui at Tielushan.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he beat rebels at Douzhenpo in Bazhou and relieved Tian Chaogui at Tielushan.

sentences.zh: 五年春，德楞泰剿冉天元於川西，檄思舉率鄉勇三千赴軍。

translations.literal: In spring of the fifth year Delengtai suppressed Ran Tianyuan in western Sichuan and ordered Siju to lead three thousand militia to the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth spring Delengtai fought Ran Tianyuan in western Sichuan and called up three thousand militia under Siju.

sentences.zh: 戰青龍口，賊踞山險，選精銳九十人夜薄賊巢，破之。

translations.literal: At Qinglong Pass rebels held perilous heights; he chose ninety elite men to press the rebel nest by night and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: At Qinglong Pass the rebels held the heights. He took ninety picked men, stormed the nest by night, and broke it.

sentences.zh: 賊分趨農安，將入陝，思舉獻計，請致書額勒登保，約守陽平關，易裝潛入賊卡，殺二賊，眾追捕，乃棄所★K7書逸出。

translations.literal: Rebels split toward Nong'an and were about to enter Shaanxi; Siju offered a plan, asked to write Ereldunbao to hold Yangping Pass, changed dress and secretly entered a rebel checkpoint, killed two rebels, was pursued by the mass, and abandoned the papers he carried and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels turned toward Nong'an and aimed for Shaanxi. Siju proposed writing Ereldunbao to hold Yangping Pass, disguised himself, slipped into a rebel post, killed two men, was chased, dropped the letter he carried, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 賊果不敢前，回竄江油。

translations.literal: The rebels truly dared not advance and turned back to flee into Jiangyou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels indeed dared not advance and doubled back into Jiangyou.

sentences.zh: 思舉先驅深入，伏起，奮鬥，而賊以擋牌禦矢銃，困德楞泰於馬蹄岡；

translations.literal: Siju advanced ahead in depth; ambush rose and he fought fiercely, while rebels used shield boards to ward off arrows and muskets and trapped Delengtai at Matigang;
translations.idiomatic: Siju pushed ahead; an ambush struck and he fought hard while rebels used shield boards against musketry and pinned Delengtai at Matigang;

sentences.zh: 急趨救，使鄉勇人取石亂擊，毀擋牌。

translations.literal: he hurried to the rescue and had militia take stones and strike at random, destroying the shield boards.
translations.idiomatic: he raced to rescue him and had militia pelt the shield boards with stones until they shattered.

sentences.zh: 會冉天元馬蹶就擒，賊瓦解。

translations.literal: At the same time Ran Tianyuan's horse stumbled and he was captured; the rebels collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Tianyuan's horse stumbled and he was taken; the rebels collapsed.

sentences.zh: 假賊旗追逐餘匪，斬雷士玉。

translations.literal: Using false rebel banners he pursued remnant bandits and beheaded Lei Shiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Flying captured rebel banners he chased the remnants and killed Lei Shiyu.

sentences.zh: 攻鮮大川於天寨子，山險不能上，德楞泰遣箭手五百助之，令伏岩下，先以鄉勇誘賊，俟擂石且盡，仰射，箭落如雨，賊退避，遂克之，思舉手擒賊六十餘人。

translations.literal: Attacking Xian Dachuan at Tianzhaizi, the mountain was perilous and could not be climbed; Delengtai sent five hundred archers to assist, ordered them to lie in ambush below the cliff, first used militia to lure rebels, waited until rolling stones were nearly exhausted, then shot upward — arrows fell like rain, rebels retreated, and it was taken; Siju personally captured more than sixty rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianzhaizi the cliffs blocked assault. Delengtai sent five hundred archers to hide below while militia baited the rebels. When the rolling stones stopped, arrows poured down; the rebels gave way and the height fell. Siju seized more than sixty men himself.

sentences.zh: 德楞泰訶其輕生，聲色俱厲；

translations.literal: Delengtai rebuked him for risking his life, voice and expression both severe;
translations.idiomatic: Delengtai scolded him for recklessness, his voice fierce;

sentences.zh: 思舉跪謝，良久出，則冠上已換花翎，由是深感德楞泰，樂為盡力。

translations.literal: Siju knelt in apology; after long while he came out and the peacock feather was already on his cap — from this he deeply felt Delengtai's favor and was glad to exert his utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Siju knelt to apologize. When he rose, a peacock plume already crowned his cap. From then on he served Delengtai with all his heart.

sentences.zh: 尋從勒保防嘉陵江，七十五以桂涵新敗，調思舉代領所部鄉勇，擢都司。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Lebao in defending the Jialing River; Qishiwu, because Gui Han had just been defeated, transferred Siju to lead his militia and promoted him to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Lebao on the Jialing. When Gui Han was beaten, Qishiwu put Siju in charge of his militia and made him battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 六年，殲張世龍於鐵溪河，擊援賊陳天奇，陣斬之，賜號蘇勒芳阿巴圖魯，擢游擊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he annihilated Zhang Shilong at Tiexi River, struck relief rebel Chen Tianqi, and killed him in the battle line; he was granted the title Sulefang'a Batu and promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he destroyed Zhang Shilong at Tiexi River, cut down the relief leader Chen Tianqi in battle, received the title Sulefang'a Batu, and was made regional commander.

sentences.zh: 自是轉戰老林，餉不時至，煮馬韉，啗賊肉以追賊。

translations.literal: From then on he fought through the old forests; rations did not arrive on time — they boiled horse girths and ate rebel flesh to pursue rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he fought in the deep forests. When rations failed they boiled saddle leather and ate rebel flesh to keep the chase.

sentences.zh: 七十五卞急，屢為賊所窘，輒賴思舉援救得捷。

translations.literal: Qishiwu was impatient and often cornered by rebels, always relying on Siju's rescue to win victories.
translations.idiomatic: Qishiwu was rash and often trapped; Siju's rescues won the day.

sentences.zh: 既而七十五坐事逮，德楞泰攻苟文明於瓦山溪，賊踞楠木坪，三戰不克。

translations.literal: Before long Qishiwu was arrested for an offense; Delengtai attacked Gou Wenming at Washanxi; rebels held Nanmuping and three battles did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Qishiwu was soon arrested. Delengtai attacked Gou Wenming at Washanxi; rebels held Nanmuping and three assaults failed.

sentences.zh: 召思舉率鄉勇至，皆衣狗皮，躡草履，人笑為匄兵，夜越後山伏，一戰破之，殲苟明獻、苟文舉。

translations.literal: Siju was summoned to lead militia; all wore dog skins and trod straw sandals — men laughed at them as beggar troops; at night they crossed the rear mountain in ambush, one battle broke the enemy, and annihilated Gou Mingxian and Gou Wenju.
translations.idiomatic: Siju was called with militia clad in dog skins and straw sandals — men mocked them as beggar troops. By night they climbed the rear slope, broke the enemy in one fight, and killed Gou Mingxian and Gou Wenju.

sentences.zh: 眾詫曰：「匄兵破賊矣！

translations.literal: The crowd exclaimed in wonder: "The beggar troops have broken the rebels!"
translations.idiomatic: Men marveled, "The beggar troops have beaten the rebels!"

sentences.zh: 」始補給餉，製衣履，擢參將。

translations.literal: " Only then were rations supplied and clothing and footwear made; he was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Only then were rations and uniforms issued. He was promoted to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 七年，迭敗庹向瑤於風硐子、萬古樓，破齊國點於通江，殲張天倫、魏學盛於巴州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he repeatedly defeated Tuo Xiangyao at Fengdongzi and Wangulou, broke Qi Guodian at Tongjiang, and annihilated Zhang Tianlun and Wei Xuesheng at Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he beat Tuo Xiangyao at Fengdongzi and Wangulou, broke Qi Guodian at Tongjiang, and destroyed Zhang Tianlun and Wei Xuesheng at Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 秋，擊劉朝選於仙女溪，遁鞋底山，擒之。

translations.literal: In autumn he struck Liu Chaoxuan at Xiannü Stream; Chaoxuan fled to Xiedishan and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn he fought Liu Chaoxuan at Xiannü Stream; Chaoxuan fled to Xiedishan and was taken.

sentences.zh: 又偕羅聲皋擒張簡、羅道荣於巴州。

translations.literal: Again with Luo Sheng'gao he captured Zhang Jian and Luo Daorong at Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: With Luo Sheng'gao he also took Zhang Jian and Luo Daorong at Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，唐明萬竄大寧，追至石柱坪，賊方食，奮擊，大潰，擒明萬。

translations.literal: In winter Tang Mingwan fled to Daning; pursued to Shizhuping, rebels were just eating — he struck fiercely and they fled in great disorder; Mingwan was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In winter Tang Mingwan fled to Daning. Siju caught him at Shizhuping while the rebels were at supper and captured Mingwan in the rout.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以明萬劇賊久稽誅，特詔嘉賚。

translations.literal: The Jiaqing Emperor, because Mingwan was a fierce rebel long eluding execution, specially edicted praise and reward.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaqing Emperor, noting that Mingwan had long defied capture, issued a special decree of praise.

sentences.zh: 諸賊漸就殲除，搜捕南山餘孽，兩年始清，擢太平協副將。

translations.literal: Rebels were gradually annihilated; searching out southern hill remnants took two years to clear; he was promoted to deputy commander of the Taiping garrison.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels were wiped out, hunting southern hill survivors took two years. He was made deputy commander at Taiping.

sentences.zh: 十年，德楞泰剿寧陝叛兵，檄思舉赴軍，尋就撫，盡釋歸伍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Delengtai suppressed the Ningshan mutineers and ordered Siju to the army; soon they were pacified and all were released back to the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Delengtai handled the Ningshan mutiny and called Siju up; the men were soon pacified and sent back to the ranks.

sentences.zh: 思舉曰：「兵變，殺將陷城破官軍，亂無大於此者。

translations.literal: Siju said: "In a mutiny one kills generals, takes cities, and breaks government troops — no disorder is greater than this."
translations.idiomatic: Siju protested, "They killed officers, stormed towns, and routed imperial troops. No crime is greater."

sentences.zh: 反賞，是勸叛也！

translations.literal: To reward them instead is to encourage rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: To reward them is to invite rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 何以懲後？

translations.literal: How can later men be deterred?"
translations.idiomatic: How will that warn those who come after?"

sentences.zh: 請誅首逆，以申國法。

translations.literal: I ask to execute the principal instigators to uphold the law of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Execute the ringleaders and uphold the law."

sentences.zh: 」諸將不可。

translations.literal: " The various generals would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals overruled him.

sentences.zh: 後川、陝兵果數叛。

translations.literal: Afterward Sichuan and Shaanxi troops indeed mutinied several times.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Sichuan and Shaanxi troops mutinied again and again.

sentences.zh: 十一年，思舉攻西鄉叛兵，斬首逆於陣，風稍息。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Siju attacked Xixiang mutineers and beheaded the principal instigator in the battle line; the wind of rebellion slightly subsided.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he attacked mutineers at Xixiang and killed their chief in battle, and the mutinous spirit cooled somewhat.

sentences.zh: 署川北鎮，擢涼州鎮總兵，未之任，調重慶鎮。

translations.literal: He acted as commander of the north Sichuan garrison, was promoted to commander of the Liangzhou garrison, did not take up the post, and was transferred to the Chongqing garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting north Sichuan commander, was promoted to Liangzhou but transferred to Chongqing before taking post.

sentences.zh: 二十年，中瞻對番酋洛布七力叛，夾河築碉。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the Zhongzan Tibetan chief Luobuqili rebelled and built stockades along the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year the Zhongzan Tibetan chief Luobuqili rebelled and built river-side forts.

sentences.zh: 總兵羅聲皋不能克，許其降，以專擅遣戍。

translations.literal: Commander Luo Sheng'gao could not take them, promised them surrender, and for acting on his own authority was exiled to garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Luo Sheng'gao failed, offered surrender on his own authority, and was exiled for overstepping.

sentences.zh: 命思舉進剿，克四砦，洛布七力就殲，請分其地以賞上下瞻對諸出力頭目，事乃定。

translations.literal: Siju was ordered to advance in suppression, took four forts, Luobuqili was destroyed, and he asked to divide the land to reward the headmen of upper and lower Zhongzan who had exerted themselves — the affair was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Siju was sent to suppress them, took four forts, destroyed Luobuqili, and divided the land among the loyal Zhongzan headmen, settling the affair.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，擢貴州提督，歷四川、雲南、湖北提督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was promoted to commander of Guizhou and served successively as commander of Sichuan, Yunnan, and Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daoguang (1821) he became commander of Guizhou and later held Sichuan, Yunnan, and Hubei.

sentences.zh: 十二年，湖南江華錦田寨瑤趙金龍為亂，與長寧趙福才糾合九衝瑤肆掠，提督海凌阿戰死，勢益熾。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Yao Zhao Jinlong of Jintian stockade in Jianghua, Hunan, raised disorder; with Changning's Zhao Fucai he gathered nine-chong Yao to plunder; Commander Hailing'a died in battle and the momentum grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (1832) the Yao leader Zhao Jinlong of Jintian stockade in Jianghua, Hunan, rebelled. With Zhao Fucai of Changning he rallied nine Yao districts to raid. Commander Hailing'a was killed and the revolt swelled.

sentences.zh: 詔總督盧坤偕思舉討之，至永州，議遏賊南竄，斷其西道州、零陵、祁陽山徑，進兵兜擊。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Governor Lu Kun with Siju to suppress them; reaching Yongzhou they planned to block the rebels' southward flight, cut their western routes through Daozhou, Lingling, and Qiyang mountain paths, and advance to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Lu Kun and Siju were ordered to suppress them. At Yongzhou they planned to block a southern flight, seal western passes through Daozhou, Lingling, and Qiyang, and strike in concert.

sentences.zh: 於是驅諸瑤出山，皆東竄常寧洋泉鎮，檄各路進逼合圍，四月，大破之，金龍中槍死，擒其妻子及死黨數十，賜雙眼花翎，予一等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: Thus the Yao were driven from the mountains; all fled east to Yangquan Town in Changning; orders went to all routes to press in and encircle; in the fourth month a great victory was won; Jinlong was shot dead; his wife, children, and several dozen diehard partisans were captured; he was granted double peacock feathers and a hereditary first-class light chariot commandant rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao were driven from the hills and fled east to Yangquan in Changning. Columns closed in; in the fourth month the rebels were shattered. Jinlong was shot dead; his family and dozens of diehards were taken. Siju received double peacock plumes and a hereditary first-class light chariot commandant rank.

sentences.zh: 時命尚書禧恩督師，未至軍，先三日奏捷。

translations.literal: At the time Minister Xien was ordered to supervise the army but had not reached it; three days before arrival he memorialized victory.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xien was appointed to command but had not arrived when victory was reported three days ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 禧恩方貴寵用事，怒其不待，盛氣陵之。

translations.literal: Xien was then in favor and wielded power; angry that Siju had not waited, he bullied him with overbearing airs.
translations.idiomatic: Xien, then powerful at court, was furious that Siju had not waited and bullied him openly.

sentences.zh: 思舉曰：「諸公貴人多顧忌。

translations.literal: Siju said: "You gentlemen of rank have many scruples."
translations.idiomatic: Siju said, "You great lords have too many scruples."

sentences.zh: 思舉一無賴，受國厚恩至提督，惟以死報，不知其他！

translations.literal: Siju is a good-for-nothing who received the state's thick favor up to commander — I repay only with death and know nothing else!"
translations.idiomatic: I was a wastrel whom the state raised to commander. I owe it nothing but my life!"

sentences.zh: 」禧恩無如何，則詰金龍死狀虛實，思舉獲其屍及所佩印、劍、木偶為證，乃止。

translations.literal: " Xien could do nothing; he then questioned whether Jinlong's death was real or false; Siju obtained his corpse and the seal, sword, and wooden puppet he carried as proof, and Xien stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xien could not answer. He challenged whether Jinlong was truly dead. Siju produced the corpse, seal, sword, and wooden charm as proof, and Xien fell silent.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒於官，賜太子太保，諡壯勇。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died in office; posthumously he was given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous title Zhuangyong (Stalwart and Valiant).
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (1840) he died in office. The court made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent posthumously and named him Zhuangyong (Stalwart and Valiant).

sentences.zh: 子本鎮，襲世職。

translations.literal: His son inherited the garrison command and the hereditary commission.
translations.idiomatic: His son Benzhen inherited the garrison post and the hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 思舉既貴，嘗與人言少時事，不少諱。

translations.literal: After Siju became eminent he would speak to others of his youth without concealing much.
translations.idiomatic: Once eminent, Siju spoke openly of his youth without shame.

sentences.zh: 檄川、陝、湖北各州縣云：「所捕盜羅思舉，今為國宣勞，可銷案矣。

translations.literal: He issued orders to magistrates of Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Hubei saying: "The bandit Luo Siju whom you captured now labors for the state — his case may be closed."
translations.idiomatic: He notified magistrates in Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Hubei: "The bandit Luo Siju you wanted is now serving the throne. Close his file."

sentences.zh: 」再入覲，仁宗問：「何省兵精？

translations.literal: On entering audience again the Jiaqing Emperor asked: "In which province are troops finest?"
translations.idiomatic: At a later audience the Jiaqing Emperor asked which province had the finest troops.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「將良兵自精。

translations.literal: " He said: "Good generals make good troops."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Good generals make good troops."

sentences.zh: 」宣宗問：「賞罰何由明？

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor asked: "How are rewards and punishments made clear?"
translations.idiomatic: The Daoguang Emperor asked how to keep rewards and punishments clear.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「進一步，賞；

translations.literal: " He said: "One step forward — reward;"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "One step forward — reward;

sentences.zh: 退一步，罰。

translations.literal: one step back — punish."
translations.idiomatic: one step back — punish."

sentences.zh: 」皆稱旨。

translations.literal: Both were praised as fitting the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Both answers pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 晚年自述年譜。

translations.literal: In his later years he wrote his own chronological autobiography.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he wrote his own chronicle.

sentences.zh: 川中殄諸劇寇，多賴其力，功為人掩，軍中與二楊並稱。

translations.literal: In Sichuan the extermination of fierce bandits relied much on his strength; merit was covered by others — in the army he was ranked with the Two Yangs.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan's worst bandits fell largely by his hand, though others took the credit. In camp he was named with the Two Yangs.

sentences.zh: 楊芳於諸將少許可，獨至思舉，以為「烈丈夫」。

translations.literal: Yang Fang seldom approved of generals; only toward Siju did he call him a "fierce true man."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fang rarely praised any general; of Siju alone he said, "a man of iron."

sentences.zh: 嘗酒酣袒身示人，戰創斑斑，為父母刲股痕凡七，其忠孝蓋出天性雲。

translations.literal: Once when drunk he bared his body to show others; battle scars were dense; marks of cutting his own flesh for his parents numbered seven in all — his filial piety and loyalty seem to have sprung from inborn nature.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk once, he bared his torso: battle scars everywhere and seven marks where he had cut his flesh for his parents — filial piety and loyalty seemed inborn.

sentences.zh: 同時起鄉勇者，桂涵名與之亞，包相卿較後出，亦至專閫。

translations.literal: Militia leaders who rose at the same time — Gui Han's fame was second to his; Bao Xiangqing came out somewhat later but also reached independent command.
translations.idiomatic: Among militia leaders of the day Gui Han ranked just below him; Bao Xiangqing came later but also rose to independent command.

sentences.zh: 涵，亦東鄉人。

translations.literal: Han was also from Dongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Han too was from Dongxiang.

sentences.zh: 少恃勇，橫行鄉里，亡命出走。

translations.literal: In youth he relied on courage and ranged tyrannically through the countryside, then fled as a fugitive.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he bullied the countryside by force and fled as an outlaw.

sentences.zh: 繼歸，與思舉同應募為鄉勇。

translations.literal: Later he returned and with Siju together answered the call as militia.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned and enlisted as militia alongside Siju.

sentences.zh: 父天聰，聚族黨屯罐子山。

translations.literal: His father Tiancong gathered clan partisans and encamped at Guanzishan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tiancong rallied clansmen and held Guanzishan.

sentences.zh: 賊數為涵所窘，欲報之，萬眾來攻。

translations.literal: Rebels were often cornered by Han and wished revenge; tens of thousands came to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels, often harried by Han, sought revenge and came in tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 涵率壯士伏隘，誘賊入空寨，痛殲之。

translations.literal: Han led stalwarts in ambush at the pass, lured rebels into an empty stockade, and annihilated them severely.
translations.idiomatic: Han ambushed the pass, lured them into an empty stockade, and slaughtered them.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年，從硃射鬥攻金峨寺，賊突出，圍涵於山峒，火熏水灌皆不傷，反多斃賊，賊乃走。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing he followed Zhu Shedou in attacking Jin'e Temple; rebels burst out and surrounded Han in a mountain cave; smoke and flooding did not harm him, and instead many rebels were killed; the rebels then fled.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing year 2 he followed Zhu Shedou at Jin'e Temple. Rebels surrounded him in a cave; smoke and flood failed to kill him and more rebels died instead.

sentences.zh: 尋戰淨土庵，偕思舉陷陣，大破之，徐天德黨眾幾盡殲。

translations.literal: Soon he fought at Jingtu'an; with Siju he charged the lines and won a great victory; Xu Tiande's partisans were nearly all annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingtu'an he and Siju charged the line and broke the enemy; Xu Tiande's band was nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 同里聞其屢捷，爭來投效，德楞泰、明亮特編涵字營，使涵領之，擢千總，由是知名。

translations.literal: Men of the same district hearing of his repeated victories vied to join; Delengtai and Mingliang specially organized the Han-character battalion for him to command; he was promoted to company commander and thus became known.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors flocked to him after each victory. Delengtai and Mingliang formed the "Han" battalion under his command and made him company commander.

sentences.zh: 三年，大軍圍安樂坪，冷天祿詐降出走，涵偵知之，伏兵於方家壩、魚鱗口，賊至伏發，擒斬甚眾，擢守備。

translations.literal: In the third year the main army besieged Anleping; Leng Tianlu feigned surrender and fled; Han learned of it by reconnaissance, set troops in ambush at Fangjiaba and Yulin Pass; rebels came and the ambush struck — many were captured or killed; he was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, when Leng Tianlu feigned surrender at Anleping, Han learned the truth, ambushed him at Fangjiaba and Yulin Pass, and was made garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 四年，從德楞泰追賊入陝，每由間道出賊前，與官軍夾擊，數捷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed Delengtai pursuing rebels into Shaanxi, often taking hidden paths ahead of the rebels to strike in concert with government troops, winning repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he followed Delengtai into Shaanxi, often cutting ahead by hidden paths to hit the rebels with the regulars.

sentences.zh: 又從硃射鬥殲包正洪於雲陽蘆花嶺。

translations.literal: Again he followed Zhu Shedou in annihilating Bao Zhenghong at Luhua Ridge in Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhu Shedou he destroyed Bao Zhenghong at Luhua Ridge in Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 從七十五破龔建於開縣火峰寨，手擒建以獻，擢都司。

translations.literal: He followed Qishiwu in defeating Gong Jian at Huofeng stockade in Kaixian, personally captured Jian and presented him, and was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: With Qishiwu he beat Gong Jian at Huofeng stockade in Kaixian, seized Jian himself, and was made battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 五年，復從射鬥破賊雲陽，擒其渠李甲，縱歸，招出黨眾數百人，自是降者日至。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again followed Shedou in breaking rebels at Yunyang, captured their leader Li Jia, released him to return, and induced several hundred partisans to come out — from then on surrenderers came daily.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again followed Shedou at Yunyang, took the chief Li Jia, released him to win over hundreds of followers, and thereafter surrenders came every day.

sentences.zh: 既而改隸勒保軍，始與思舉分路，轉戰川東西，所至有功，累擢游擊。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Lebao's army, first separated routes with Siju, fought east and west in Sichuan, had merit wherever he went, and was repeatedly promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was then assigned to Lebao, operated apart from Siju, campaigned across eastern and western Sichuan with steady success, and rose to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 六年，從阿哈保追湯思蛟於墊江，賊夜走，涵謂：「窮寇且死鬥，請先伏魏家溝。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Ahobao in pursuing Tang Sijiao at Dianjiang; rebels fled by night; Han said: "Cornered bandits will fight to the death — please first set an ambush at Weijiagou."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he followed Ahobao after Tang Sijiao at Dianjiang. The rebels fled by night. Han said, "Cornered men will fight to the death. Ambush them at Weijiagou."

sentences.zh: 」俟其至，突擊，大破之。

translations.literal: " When they arrived he charged suddenly and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: When they came he struck and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 又從薛大烈追李彬、冉天士於通江，至小中河，大雪，賊不為備，涵率鄉勇夜半薄賊壘，與官軍四面乘之，賊奔曠野，勁騎衝踏，盡殲焉。

translations.literal: Again he followed Xue Dalie in pursuing Li Bin and Ran Tianshi at Tongjiang; reaching Xiaozhong River, heavy snow fell and rebels were unprepared; Han led militia at midnight to press the rebel camp, government troops struck from four sides, rebels fled to open country, fierce cavalry charged and trampled, and all were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: With Xue Dalie he chased Li Bin and Ran Tianshi to Tongjiang. At Xiaozhong River a snowstorm caught the rebels off guard. Han led militia at midnight against the camp while regulars closed from four sides. The enemy broke into the open and were trampled down by cavalry until none remained.

sentences.zh: 彬遁，未幾，為劉清所獲。

translations.literal: Bin escaped; before long he was captured by Liu Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Bin escaped but was soon taken by Liu Qing.

sentences.zh: 自七年後，复偕思舉遍歷老林，搜剿匿匪，累遷夔州協副將。

translations.literal: From the seventh year onward he again joined Siju in traversing the old forests, searching out and suppressing hidden bandits, and was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the Kuizhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: From the seventh year on he again ranged the deep forests with Siju, rooting out hidden bandits, and rose to deputy commander at Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 九年秋，從經略、參贊圍餘匪於太平火燒梁山，峻無路。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year he followed the grand coordinator and commissioner in besieging remnant bandits at Taiping Huoshaoliang Mountain, steep with no road.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth autumn he joined the grand coordinator's siege of remnant bandits on Huoshaoliang at Taiping — cliffs with no path.

sentences.zh: 涵議：「守此相持，雖數月無如賊何。

translations.literal: Han proposed: "Holding here in stalemate, even for several months nothing can be done with the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Han argued, "A stalemate here will not break them even in months."

sentences.zh: 山下小溪通民峒，賊久困，必出劫峒糧，請以步卒伏山後。

translations.literal: A small stream below the mountain connects to civilian cave hamlets; rebels long besieged will surely come out to raid cave grain — I ask to place foot soldiers in ambush behind the mountain."
translations.idiomatic: A stream below leads to civilian cave hamlets. Starved rebels will raid for grain. Put infantry in ambush behind the ridge."

sentences.zh: 」賊果以驍銳千餘潛出，諸將皆死戰，半日殲之，前山自潰。

translations.literal: " Rebels truly sent more than a thousand elite men out secretly; all generals fought to the death; in half a day they were annihilated, and the forward mountain collapsed of itself.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand elite rebels slipped out as he foretold. The generals fought to the last; by midday they were destroyed and the forward slope gave way.

sentences.zh: 遂殄滅淨盡，川、陝肅清。

translations.literal: They were then exterminated clean; Sichuan and Shaanxi were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The last bands were wiped out and Sichuan and Shaanxi were cleared.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，綏定兵叛，涵在梁山聞變，慮本部兵與通，單騎馳入郡城，聲言越兩日出兵；

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year Suining troops mutinied; Han was at Liangshan when he heard, feared his own troops would communicate with them, and rode alone into the prefectural city, declaring troops would march in two days;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh winter Suining troops mutinied. Han was at Liangshan, feared his own men would join them, rode alone into the prefectural city, and announced a march in two days;

sentences.zh: 密令弟吉出募鄉勇舊部為一隊，約期合攻。

translations.literal: secretly ordered his younger brother Ji to go out and recruit former militia subordinates as one company, fixing a date for a joint attack.
translations.idiomatic: he secretly told his brother Ji to raise his old militia company for a joint strike on a set day.

sentences.zh: 時賊踞景市廟，將往麻柳場。

translations.literal: At the time rebels held Jingshi Temple and were about to go to Maliuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Jingshi Temple and were heading for Maliuchang.

sentences.zh: 涵至，令急赴景市廟，中途改趨麻柳場，距賊數里止隊，入深箐，諜報賊逾千，且至，叱曰：「安得有此眾？

translations.literal: When Han arrived he ordered haste to Jingshi Temple, then midway changed toward Maliuchang, halted the column several li from the rebels, entered a deep ravine; spies reported more than a thousand rebels approaching; he rebuked: "How could there be so many?"
translations.idiomatic: Han ordered a rush to Jingshi Temple, then swung toward Maliuchang, halted a few li short, and entered a ravine. Scouts reported a thousand rebels. He snapped, "Impossible!"

sentences.zh: 」戒毋輕進，毋漏言涵至。

translations.literal: " He warned not to advance lightly and not to leak word that Han had come.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade a rash advance and forbade mention of his arrival.

sentences.zh: 既而賊自山沖下，三進三退，乃突起擊賊；

translations.literal: Before long rebels charged down from the mountain; three advances and three retreats — then he suddenly rose and struck the rebels;
translations.idiomatic: Rebels charged downhill. After three feints he sprang the attack;

sentences.zh: 而弟吉已率五百人據山頂，賊大潰，擒首逆王德先。

translations.literal: while his younger brother Ji had already led five hundred men to hold the hilltop; rebels fled in great disorder and the principal instigator Wang Dexian was captured.
translations.idiomatic: his brother Ji already held the summit with five hundred men. The rebels broke; the ringleader Wang Dexian was taken.

sentences.zh: 叛兵起事甫五日，一鼓平之，賜號健勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: The mutiny had risen only five days before; one drumbeat pacified it; he was granted the title Vigorous Brave Batu.
translations.idiomatic: The mutiny was only five days old; one stroke ended it. He received the title Vigorous Brave Batu.

sentences.zh: 十三年，署重慶鎮，尋授川北鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he acted as commander of the Chongqing garrison and soon was appointed commander of the north Sichuan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he acted at Chongqing and soon became north Sichuan commander.

sentences.zh: 十九年，擊三才峽匪黨吳抓抓等於沔縣，走之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he struck Sancai Gorge bandit partisans Wu Zhuazhua and others at Mianxian and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he drove Sancai Gorge bandits such as Wu Zhuazhua from Mianxian.

sentences.zh: 川北獲安。

translations.literal: North Sichuan was secured.
translations.idiomatic: North Sichuan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，擢四川提督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he was promoted to commander of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daoguang (1822) he became commander of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 果洛克番匪劫西藏堪布貢物，命剿擒首逆曲俊父子，被優賚。

translations.literal: Golok Tibetan bandits robbed tribute goods of a Tibetan khubilgan; he was ordered to suppress and capture the principal instigators Qujun father and son, and received generous reward.
translations.idiomatic: Golok Tibetans robbed a khubilgan's tribute caravan. He was ordered to capture the chiefs Qujun and his son and was richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 在任十載，遇番、夷蠢動，兵至輒定。

translations.literal: In office ten years; whenever Tibetans or tribes stirred, troops arrived and it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years in office, whenever border tribes stirred, his troops arrived and the trouble ended.

sentences.zh: 十三年，討越巂夷匪，連戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he suppressed Yuexi tribal bandits and won every battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he fought Yuexi tribal rebels and won every engagement.

sentences.zh: 忽遘疾，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Suddenly he fell ill and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He fell suddenly ill and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 優恤，贈太子太保，諡壯勇。

translations.literal: Favorable condolence was granted; posthumously he was given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous title Zhuangyong (Stalwart and Valiant).
translations.idiomatic: The court granted generous mourning benefits, made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent posthumously, and named him Zhuangyong (Stalwart and Valiant).

sentences.zh: 子三人，並晉官秩。

translations.literal: Three sons all received advancement in rank.
translations.idiomatic: All three sons received promotions in rank.

sentences.zh: 相卿，鄰水人。

translations.literal: Xiangqing was a man of Linshui.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangqing came from Linshui.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年，以鄉勇隸松潘鎮標。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he joined the Songpan garrison standard as militia.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he entered the Songpan garrison corps as militia.

sentences.zh: 嘗從思舉擊陳朝觀於通江龍鳳埡，追賊受矛傷，裹創力戰。

translations.literal: He once followed Siju in striking Chen Chaoguan at Longfeng'ya in Tongjiang, pursued rebels and was wounded by a spear, fought on with bandaged wounds.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Siju against Chen Chaoguan at Longfeng'ya in Tongjiang, took a spear wound in the pursuit, and fought on with bandaged wounds.

sentences.zh: 七年，破張天倫於巴州金子寺，相卿斬天倫轂子山下，給藍翎、八品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he defeated Zhang Tianlun at Jinzi Temple in Bazhou; Xiangqing beheaded Tianlun below Guzishan and was given blue feather and eighth-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he helped break Zhang Tianlun at Jinzi Temple in Bazhou. Xiangqing cut down Tianlun below Guzishan and received the blue plume and eighth-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 又殲張簡、唐明萬，功皆最。

translations.literal: Again he annihilated Zhang Jian and Tang Mingwan; his merit ranked foremost.
translations.idiomatic: He also destroyed Zhang Jian and Tang Mingwan, topping the merit rolls again.

sentences.zh: 十年，思舉偵襄賊王世貴、謝應洪匿太平老林，檄相卿躡捕，殲之，授千總。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Siju learned Xiangyang rebels Wang Shigui and Xie Yinghong were hiding in the Taiping old forest and ordered Xiangqing to pursue and capture them; they were annihilated; he was appointed company commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Siju learned Wang Shigui and Xie Yinghong were hiding in the Taiping forest and sent Xiangqing to destroy them. He was made company commander.

sentences.zh: 十二年，剿瓦石坪叛兵，擢守備。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he suppressed Washiping mutineers and was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he put down the Washiping mutiny and became garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 累遷廣元營游擊。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to regional commander of the Guangyuan battalion.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to regional commander of the Guangyuan battalion.

sentences.zh: 十三年，調徵台灣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred for campaign in Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was ordered to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 會峨邊越巂倮夷叛，命回川從提督楊芳赴剿，攻克啯嚕崖。

translations.literal: It happened that Ebian and Yuexi Lolo tribes rebelled; he was ordered back to Sichuan to follow Commander Yang Fang in suppression and stormed Guluya cliff.
translations.idiomatic: Ebian and Yuexi Lolo tribes rebelled; he was recalled to follow Yang Fang, stormed Guluya cliff, and returned to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 夷踞曲曲烏烏斯坡，相卿梯絕壁，牽挽負砲而上，破之，進毀巴姑賊寨，擢參將。

translations.literal: Tribes held Ququwuwusi slope; Xiangqing scaled the sheer cliff, hauled and carried cannon up, broke them, advanced and destroyed the Bagu rebel stockade, and was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes held Ququwuwusi slope. Xiangqing climbed the cliff, hauled guns up, broke them, burned the Bagu stockade, and was made deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 十五年，倮夷复叛，攻克峨邊十三支夷巢，破越巂沈喳夷，抵濫田壩，兩廳叛夷悉降，累遷懋功協副將。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Lolo tribes rebelled again; he stormed thirteen tribal nests at Ebian, broke Yuexi Shenzha tribes, reached Lantianba, and rebels of both districts all surrendered; he was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the Maogong garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the Lolo rebelled again. He took thirteen Ebian nests, broke the Yuexi Shenzha, reached Lantianba, and pacified both districts. He rose to deputy commander at Maogong.

sentences.zh: 剿馬邊夷，擒其渠，加總兵銜。

translations.literal: Suppressing Mabian tribes he captured their chief and was given the additional rank of commander.
translations.idiomatic: Against Mabian tribes he took their chief and received the additional rank of commander.

sentences.zh: 再署建昌鎮總兵，總督鄂山、寶興皆以邊事倚之。

translations.literal: Again he acted as commander of the Jianchang garrison; Governors Eshan and Baoxing both relied on him for frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He again acted as Jianchang commander; Governors Eshan and Baoxing both relied on him for the border.

sentences.zh: 十九年，病歸，卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he returned home ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he went home sick and died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：川、楚之役，竭宇內之兵力而後定之。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The Sichuan-Hubei campaign exhausted the empire's military strength before it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: The Sichuan-Hubei war drained the empire's armies before peace came.

sentences.zh: 材武驍猛，萃於行間，然戰無不勝，攻無不取者，厥惟二楊及羅思舉為之冠。

translations.literal: Men of martial talent and fierce bravery gathered in the ranks; yet those who never lost a battle or failed in an assault were headed by the Two Yangs and Luo Siju.
translations.idiomatic: Brave fighters filled the ranks, yet none matched the Two Yangs and Luo Siju for winning every fight.

sentences.zh: 遇春謀勇俱絕，劇寇半為所殲。

translations.literal: Yuchun's strategy and courage were unsurpassed; half the fierce bandits were destroyed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchun's counsel and courage were unmatched; he destroyed half the worst rebels himself.

sentences.zh: 思舉習於賊情、地勢、險阨，強梁非其莫克。

translations.literal: Siju was versed in rebel ways, terrain, and perilous passes — the violent and strong none but he could subdue.
translations.idiomatic: Siju knew rebel habits, ground, and passes — none could master the hardest foes but he.

sentences.zh: 至於忠誠忘私，身名俱泰，遇春際遇之隆，固為稀覯；

translations.literal: As for loyal devotion forgetting self-interest, body and fame both flourishing — Yuchun's exalted fortune was indeed rarely seen;
translations.idiomatic: In loyalty and selflessness, fame and fortune together — Yuchun's rise was rare;

sentences.zh: 而思舉以藪澤梟傑，終保令名，煥於旂常矣。

translations.literal: yet Siju, a hero of marshes and thickets, in the end preserved a good name and shines on the battle banners.
translations.idiomatic: yet Siju, a outlaw made general, kept his honor bright on the colors.

sentences.zh: 鄉兵出平鉅寇，亦自其為始雲。

translations.literal: Militia sent out to pacify great bandits — it began with them.
translations.idiomatic: The use of militia to crush great rebels began with these men.
